title.zh: 卷四百十六 列傳第一百七十五 吳淵 余玠 汪立信 向士璧 胡穎 冷應澂 曹叔遠 王萬 馬光祖
title.en: Volume 416 Biographies 175: Wu Yuan, Yu Jie, Wang Lixin, Xiang Shibi, Hu Ying, Leng Yingcheng, Cao Shuyuan, Wang Wan, Ma Guangzu
title.raw: 卷四百十六 列傳第一百七十五 吳淵 余玠 汪立信 向士璧 胡穎 冷應澂 曹叔遠 王萬 馬光祖 Volume 416 Biographies 175: Wu Yuan, Yu Jie, Wang Lixin, Xiang Shibi, Hu Ying, Leng Yingcheng, Cao Shuyuan, Wang Wan, Ma Guangzu

sentences.zh: 吳淵餘玠汪立信向士璧胡穎冷應澂曹叔遠

translations.literal: Wu Yuan, Yu Jie, Wang Lixin, Xiang Shibi, Hu Ying, Leng Yingcheng, and Cao Shuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuan, Yu Jie, Wang Lixin, Xiang Shibi, Hu Ying, Leng Yingcheng, and Cao Shuyuan.

sentences.zh: 〈（從子豳）〉

translations.literal: (the nephew Bin)
translations.idiomatic: (nephew Bin)

sentences.zh: 王萬馬光祖

translations.literal: Wang Wan and Ma Guangzu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan and Ma Guangzu.

sentences.zh: 吳淵，字道父，秘閣修撰柔勝之第三子也。

translations.literal: Wu Yuan, styled Daofu, was the third son of the Secretariat Compiler Rou Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuan, whose style was Daofu, was the third son of Rou Sheng, a Secretariat Compiler.

sentences.zh: 幼端重寡言，苦誌力學。

translations.literal: In youth he was dignified and serious, spoke little, and studied hard with determination.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was grave and reserved, spoke little, and threw himself into his studies.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪母，哭 泣哀慕如成人。

translations.literal: At five he lost his mother and wept and mourned with grief like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five his mother died, and he wept and grieved with the sorrow of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年舉進士，調建德縣主簿，丞相史彌遠館留之，語竟日，大悅，謂淵曰：“君，國器也，今開化新置尉，即日可上，欲以此處君。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as Registrar of Jiande County. The Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan kept him as a guest at his residence and talked with him all day, greatly pleased, and said to Yuan: "You are a pillar of the state. Kaihua has newly established a bailiff post that can be filled at once; I wish to place you there.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jiading reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Jiande County. Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan had him stay at his residence as a guest; they talked all day, and Miyuan was greatly pleased. He said to Yuan, "You are material for the nation's service. Kaihua has just created a bailiff's post that can be filled immediately, and I would like to put you there.

sentences.zh: ”淵對 曰：“甫得一官，何敢躁進，況家有嚴君，所當稟命。

translations.literal: " Yuan replied: "Having only just obtained one office, how dare I press for advancement? Moreover I have a strict father at home to whom I ought to report.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan answered, "I have only just received one post—how dare I push for promotion? Besides, I have a stern father at home whose permission I must seek.

sentences.zh: ”彌遠為之改容，不復強。

translations.literal: " Miyuan changed his expression toward him and did not press further.
translations.idiomatic: " Miyuan's manner changed, and he did not insist.

sentences.zh: 至官，就辟令。

translations.literal: When he reached his post, he accepted appointment as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up his post, he accepted appointment as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 江東九郡之冤，訟於諸使者，皆乞送淵。

translations.literal: Wronged parties from the nine prefectures of Jiangdong who brought lawsuits before the various commissioners all asked that their cases be sent to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: People with grievances from the nine Jiangdong prefectures who sued before the various commissioners all asked that their cases be referred to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 改差浙東製置使司幹辦公 事。

translations.literal: He was transferred as administrative clerk of the Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as an administrative clerk in the Eastern Zhejiang Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，詔以前職起復，力辭，弗許，再辭，且貽書政府曰：“人道莫大於事親，事親莫大於送死，苟冒哀求榮，則平生大節已掃地矣，他日何以 事君？

translations.literal: On his father's death he entered mourning. An edict ordered him recalled to his former post; he strenuously declined but was not permitted. He declined again and sent a letter to the government saying: "Nothing in human conduct is greater than serving one's parents, and nothing in serving one's parents is greater than performing their funeral rites. If one presumptuously seeks favor while still in mourning, one's fundamental integrity is swept away—how could one serve one's ruler in the future?
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning. An edict recalled him to his former post; he refused firmly but was not allowed to. He refused again and wrote to the government: "Nothing in human duty exceeds serving one's parents, and nothing in serving one's parents exceeds seeing them properly buried. If I presumptuously beg for honor while still in mourning, the great integrity of my life is already gone—how could I serve my ruler afterward?

sentences.zh: ”時丞相史嵩之方起復，或曰：“得無礙時宰乎？

translations.literal: " At that time Chief Councilor Shi Songzhi was also being recalled from mourning, and someone said: "Will this not offend the chief minister?
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Chief Councilor Shi Songzhi was also being recalled from mourning, and someone said, "Will this not get in the way of the chief minister?

sentences.zh: ”淵弗顧，詔從之。

translations.literal: " Yuan paid no heed; the edict followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan paid no attention; the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 服除，差浙東提舉茶鹽司幹辦公事，尋改鎮江府節製司、沿江製置使司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was assigned as administrative clerk of the Eastern Zhejiang Tea and Salt Intendant, and soon after transferred to administrative clerk of the Zhenjiang Military Commission and the Riverine Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was posted as clerk in the Eastern Zhejiang Tea and Salt Intendant's office, and soon after as clerk in the Zhenjiang Military Commission and the Riverine Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 皆不 就。

translations.literal: He accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of these posts.

sentences.zh: 知武陵縣，改揚子縣兼淮東轉運司幹辦公事，添差通判真州。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Wuling County, then was transferred to Yangzi County while also serving as administrative clerk of the Huaidong Transport Commission, and was additionally assigned as Vice-Prefect of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wuling County, then Yangzi County while also serving as clerk of the Huaidong Transport Commission, and was given an additional assignment as vice-prefect of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為將作監丞，遷樞密院編修官兼刑部郎官，再遷秘書丞仍兼刑部郎官。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice-Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, was promoted to Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as Vice Minister of Justice, and was promoted again to Secretary while still holding the post at the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as vice-director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, then promoted to compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as vice minister of justice, and again to secretary while retaining his justice post.

sentences.zh: 以直煥章閣知平江府兼節 製許浦水軍，提點浙西刑獄。

translations.literal: With the rank of Direct Attendant of the Hall for the Illumination of Literature he governed Pingjiang Prefecture while also commanding the Xupu Naval Forces and serving as Judicial Intendant of Western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: As Direct Attendant of the Hall for the Illumination of Literature he governed Pingjiang Prefecture, commanded the Xupu naval forces, and served as judicial intendant of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 會衢、嚴盜起，警報至，調遣將士招捕之，殲其渠魁，散其支黨，以功為樞密院檢詳諸房文字兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢 討官兼左司。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Qu and Yan prefectures and alarms arrived, he deployed officers and soldiers to pursue and capture them, destroyed their ringleaders, and dispersed their followers. For this merit he was made Examiner of Documents in all sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as Compiler at the National History Office, Examiner at the Veritable Records Office, and concurrently in the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out in Qu and Yan and alarms reached him, he dispatched troops to hunt them down, killed their leaders, and broke up their bands. For this he was made examiner of documents in all sections of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with concurrent posts as compiler at the National History Office, examiner at the Veritable Records Office, and in the Left Section.

sentences.zh: 進右文殿修撰、樞密副都承旨兼右司兼檢正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Right Culture, Deputy Chief Receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving in the Right Section and as Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall of Right Culture, deputy chief receptionist of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with concurrent duties in the Right Section and as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 適政府欲用兵中原、以據關守河為說，淵力陳其不可，大要謂“國家力決不能取，縱取之決不能守”，丞 相鄭清之不樂而罷。

translations.literal: Just then the government wished to use force in the Central Plains, arguing that holding the passes and guarding the Yellow River would suffice. Yuan strongly argued that this could not be done, stating in essence that "the state by its strength certainly cannot take them, and even if it took them it certainly cannot hold them." Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi was displeased and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the government wanted to campaign in the Central Plains on the argument that seizing the passes and holding the Yellow River would be enough. Yuan argued forcefully against it, saying in effect that the dynasty lacked the strength to conquer the region and, even if it did, could not hold it. Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi took offense and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 出知江州，改江、淮、荊、浙、福建、廣南都大提點坑冶，都司袁商令御史王定劾淵，罷。

translations.literal: He was sent out to govern Jiang Prefecture, then was changed to Grand Intendant of Mining Smelting for Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guangnan. Yuan Shang of the Chief Office had Censor Wang Ding impeach Yuan, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to govern Jiang Prefecture, then reassigned as grand intendant of mining and smelting for Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guangnan. Yuan Shang of the chief office had Censor Wang Ding impeach him, and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 侍御史洪谘夔不直之，劾定左遷。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Hong Zikui considered this unjust and impeached Ding, who was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Hong Zikui thought this unfair and impeached Wang Ding, who was demoted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邊事果如淵 言，清之致書引咎巽謝。

translations.literal: Before long the frontier affairs turned out exactly as Yuan had said, and Qingzhi sent a letter acknowledging fault and humbly apologizing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the border situation unfolded exactly as Yuan had predicted, and Qingzhi wrote to admit his error and apologize humbly.

sentences.zh: 差知鎮江府，定防江軍之擾，兼淮弄清總領，以功遷太府少卿，復以總領兼知鎮江，加集英殿修撰、知鎮江兼總領。

translations.literal: He was assigned to govern Zhenjiang Prefecture, settled disturbances among the river-defense troops, and concurrently served as overall controller of Huaiqing. For his merit he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, again served as overall controller while also governing Zhenjiang, and was given the additional rank of Academician of the Hall of Assembled Excellence while governing Zhenjiang and serving as overall controller.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to govern Zhenjiang, quelled trouble among the river-defense troops, and concurrently served as overall controller of Huaiqing supplies. For this he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then again made overall controller while governing Zhenjiang, with the added title of academician of the Hall of Assembled Excellence.

sentences.zh: 進權工部侍郎，職任如 舊。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Works with duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice minister of works, with his duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 權兵部侍郎，權戶部侍郎，再為總領兼知鎮江。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Vice Minister of War, Acting Vice Minister of Revenue, and again as overall controller while also governing Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of war, then acting vice minister of revenue, and again as overall controller while governing Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 時淵造闕下入對，曆陳九事，甫下殿，御史唐璘擊之，璘蓋淵所薦者也。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan came to the palace to answer the emperor's questions and set forth nine matters in succession. He had just left the hall when Censor Tang Lin attacked him—Lin was in fact someone Yuan had recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then came to court to answer the emperor's questions and laid out nine points in turn. He had barely left the hall when Censor Tang Lin impeached him—Lin was someone Yuan himself had recommended.

sentences.zh: 遂仍前職，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was therefore restored to his former duties and made Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore returned to his former post and made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，加寶章閣待制，再起知鎮江兼總領。

translations.literal: After a long while he was given the rank of Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Treasured Documents and was again appointed to govern Zhenjiang while also serving as overall controller.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was given the rank of attendant-in-waiting of the Hall of Treasured Documents and was again appointed to govern Zhenjiang while serving as overall controller.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以戶部侍郎兼知鎮江府，召赴行在。

translations.literal: Before long, as Vice Minister of Revenue while also governing Zhenjiang Prefecture, he was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, as vice minister of revenue while also governing Zhenjiang, he was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣直學士知太平州，尋兼江東轉運使。

translations.literal: With the rank of Direct Academician of the Hall of Treasured Documents he governed Taiping Prefecture, and soon after also served as Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: As direct academician of the Hall of Treasured Documents he governed Taiping Prefecture, and soon afterward also served as Jiangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮民流徙入境者四十餘萬，淵亟加慰撫而賙濟之，使之什伍，令土著人無相犯。

translations.literal: At that time more than four hundred thousand people from the two Huai regions had fled into his jurisdiction. Yuan urgently comforted and relieved them, organized them in groups of ten and five, and ordered the local inhabitants not to molest one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than four hundred thousand refugees from the two Huai regions had streamed into his territory. Yuan quickly comforted and aided them, organized them in groups of ten and five, and ordered the local people not to harm one another.

sentences.zh: 旁郡流民焚劫無虛日，獨太平境內肅然無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: In neighboring prefectures refugees looted and burned almost daily, but within Taiping alone all was orderly and none dared make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In neighboring prefectures refugees burned and plundered almost every day, but within Taiping alone all was quiet and no one dared make a disturbance.

sentences.zh: 以功加華文閣直學士、沿海 製置使、知慶元府，不赴；

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the rank of Direct Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, made Coastal Pacification Commissioner, and appointed to govern Qingyuan Prefecture, but he did not go;
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made direct academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, coastal pacification commissioner, and governor of Qingyuan Prefecture, but he did not take up the post;

sentences.zh: 以工部尚書、沿海製置副使知江州，亦不赴。

translations.literal: he was then made Minister of Works, Deputy Coastal Pacification Commissioner, and Governor of Jiang Prefecture, but again he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: he was then made minister of works, deputy coastal pacification commissioner, and governor of Jiang Prefecture, but again declined.

sentences.zh: 升華文閣學士、知隆興府、江西安撫使兼轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, appointed to govern Longxing Prefecture, and made Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner while also serving as Deputy Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall of Literary Glory, appointed to govern Longxing Prefecture, and made Jiangxi pacification commissioner while also serving as deputy transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會歲大侵，講行荒政，全活者七十八萬 九千餘人。

translations.literal: When a great famine occurred he carried out famine relief policies and saved the lives of more than seven hundred eighty-nine thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: When a severe famine struck he put famine relief measures into effect and kept more than seven hundred eighty-nine thousand people alive.

sentences.zh: 徙知潭州、湖南安撫使，不赴，加敷文閣學士，仍知隆興府，安撫、轉運副使如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Tan Prefecture and serve as Hunan Pacification Commissioner but did not go. He was given the rank of Academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and continued to govern Longxing Prefecture with his pacification and deputy transport posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Tan Prefecture and serve as Hunan pacification commissioner but did not go. He was given the rank of academician of the Hall of Dispersed Literature and continued at Longxing with his pacification and deputy transport duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 改知鎮江府兼都大提舉浙西沿海諸州軍、許浦、澉浦等處兵船，歲亦 大侵，因淵全活者六十五萬八千餘人。

translations.literal: He was changed to govern Zhenjiang Prefecture while also serving as Grand Intendant of naval vessels for the coastal prefectures and military districts of western Zhejiang, Xupu, Ganpu, and other places. That year too there was a great famine, and through Yuan more than six hundred fifty-eight thousand people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern Zhenjiang while also serving as grand intendant of naval forces for the coastal prefectures and districts of western Zhejiang, Xupu, Ganpu, and elsewhere. That year too there was a great famine, and through Yuan more than six hundred fifty-eight thousand people were kept alive.

sentences.zh: 右正言三疏劾淵，奪職。

translations.literal: The Right Remonstrator submitted three memorials impeaching Yuan, and his office was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: The right remonstrator submitted three memorials impeaching Yuan, and he was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋復職，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Before long his office was restored and he was made Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his office was restored and he was made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，進龍圖閣學士、江西安撫 使兼知江州，尋為沿江製置副使兼提舉南康軍兵甲公事、節製蘄黃州、安慶府屯田使。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he entered mourning. When mourning ended he was promoted to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, made Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner while also governing Jiang Prefecture, and soon after served as Deputy Riverine Pacification Commissioner while also supervising military affairs of Nankang Army, commanding Qizhou and Huangzhou, and serving as Agricultural Intendant of Anqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he entered mourning. When mourning ended he was promoted to academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, made Jiangxi pacification commissioner while also governing Jiang Prefecture, and soon afterward served as deputy riverine pacification commissioner while supervising military affairs of Nankang Army, commanding Qi and Huang prefectures, and serving as agricultural intendant of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 湖南峒寇蔓入江右之境，破數縣，袁、洪大震，淵命將調兵，生禽其渠魁，亂 遂平。

translations.literal: Hunan cave-bandits spread into the Jiangyou region, overran several counties, and Yuan and Hong prefectures were greatly shaken. Yuan ordered generals to mobilize troops, captured their ringleaders alive, and the disorder was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan cave rebels spread into Jiangyou, overran several counties, and threw Yuan and Hong prefectures into alarm. Yuan ordered his generals to mobilize troops, took the rebel leaders alive, and the disturbance was put down.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書、知平江府兼浙西兩淮發運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War, governing Pingjiang Prefecture while also serving as Transport Commissioner for Western Zhejiang and the two Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of war, governing Pingjiang while also serving as transport commissioner for western Zhejiang and the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 尋兼知平江府，歲亦大侵，因淵全活者四十二萬三千五百餘人。

translations.literal: Soon after he also governed Pingjiang Prefecture. That year too there was a great famine, and through Yuan more than four hundred twenty-three thousand five hundred people were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also governing Pingjiang. That year too there was a great famine, and through Yuan more than four hundred twenty-three thousand five hundred people were kept alive.

sentences.zh: 兼浙西提點刑獄、知太平州兼提領兩淮茶鹽所，以 功進端明殿學士、沿江製置使、江東安撫使兼知建康府、兼行宮留守、節製和州無為軍安慶府兼三郡屯田使。

translations.literal: He also served as Judicial Intendant of Western Zhejiang, governed Taiping Prefecture while supervising the Two Huai Tea and Salt Office, and for his merit was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, made Riverine Pacification Commissioner and Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner while also governing Jiankang Prefecture, serving as Mobile Court Garrison Commander, commanding Hezhou, Wuwei Army, and Anqing Prefecture, and serving as Agricultural Intendant of three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as judicial intendant of western Zhejiang, governed Taiping while supervising the Two Huai tea and salt office, and for his merit was promoted to academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, made riverine pacification commissioner and Jiangdong pacification commissioner while governing Jiankang, serving as mobile-court garrison commander, commanding He Prefecture, Wuwei Army, and Anqing, and serving as agricultural intendant of three jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷付淵以光、豐、蘄、黃之事，凡創司 空山燕家山金剛台三大砦、嵯峨山膺山什子山等二十二小砦，團丁壯置軍，分立隊伍，星聯棋布，脈絡貫通，無事則耕，有警則禦。

translations.literal: The court entrusted Yuan with affairs in Guang, Feng, Qi, and Huang. In all he established three great stockades at Kongshan, Yanjiashan, and Jingangtai, and twenty-two smaller stockades at Cuo'e Mountain, Ying Mountain, Shizi Mountain, and elsewhere. He organized able-bodied men into militia units, divided them into companies arranged like stars on a board with connecting veins, so that in peace they farmed and in alarm they defended.
translations.idiomatic: The court entrusted Yuan with affairs in Guang, Feng, Qi, and Huang. He established three major stockades at Kongshan, Yanjiashan, and Jingangtai, and twenty-two smaller ones at Cuo'e Mountain, Ying Mountain, Shizi Mountain, and elsewhere. He organized able-bodied men into militia units in separate companies, arrayed like stars on a chessboard with every link connected, so that in peace they farmed and in alarm they fought.

sentences.zh: 詔以淵興利除害所列二十有五 事，究心軍民，拜資政殿大學士，職任如舊，與執政恩例，封金陵侯，復賜“錦繡堂”、“忠勤樓”大字。

translations.literal: An edict cited the twenty-five matters Yuan had listed for promoting benefit and removing harm, noted his devoted care for army and people, and appointed him Grand Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance with duties unchanged, granting him the privileges of a chief councilor, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Jinling, and again bestowing the large characters "Brocade Hall" and "Loyal and Diligent Tower."
translations.idiomatic: An edict cited the twenty-five measures Yuan had proposed for public benefit, praised his devoted care for soldiers and civilians, and made him grand academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance with duties unchanged, granting him the privileges of a chief councilor, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Jinling, and again bestowing the large plaques "Brocade Hall" and "Loyal and Diligent Tower."

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，徙知福州、福建安撫使。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to duke, and he was transferred to govern Fuzhou and serve as Fujian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His noble rank was raised to duke, and he was transferred to govern Fuzhou and serve as Fujian pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 改知平江府兼發運 使。

translations.literal: He was changed to govern Pingjiang Prefecture while also serving as Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern Pingjiang while also serving as transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 御史劉元龍劾淵，帝寢其奏，改知寧國府。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Yuanlong impeached Yuan, but the emperor shelved the memorial and transferred Yuan to govern Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Yuanlong impeached Yuan, but the emperor set the memorial aside and transferred him to govern Ningguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累具辭免，且丐祠，以本官提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted requests to decline and also begged for a sinecure post, and was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace with his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to be relieved and begged for a sinecure, and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 起知潭州、湖南安撫使，不赴。

translations.literal: He was recalled to govern Tan Prefecture and serve as Hunan Pacification Commissioner but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Tan Prefecture and serve as Hunan pacification commissioner but did not go.

sentences.zh: 改知太平兼提領江、淮茶鹽 所，轉荊湖製置大使、知江陵府兼夔路策應大使，兼京湖屯田大使，帶行京湖安撫製置大使。

translations.literal: He was changed to govern Taiping while supervising the Jiang and Huai Tea and Salt Office, then transferred to Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu, Governor of Jiangling Prefecture while also serving as Grand Coordinator for Kuizhou Circuit, Grand Agricultural Intendant of Jinghu, and concurrently acting Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to govern Taiping while supervising the Jiang and Huai tea and salt office, then made grand pacification commissioner of Jinghu, governor of Jiangling while also serving as grand coordinator for Kuizhou circuit, grand agricultural intendant of Jinghu, and concurrently acting grand pacification commissioner of Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 拜觀文殿學士，職任如舊，兼總領湖廣江西京西財賦、湖北京西軍馬錢 糧。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture with duties unchanged, and also served as overall controller of revenues for Huguang, Jiangxi, and Jingxi, and of funds for troops and horses in northern Huguang and Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture with duties unchanged, and also served as overall controller of revenues for Huguang, Jiangxi, and Jingxi and of funds for troops and horses in northern Huguang and Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 淵調兵二萬往援川蜀，其後力戰於白河、沮河、玉泉。

translations.literal: Yuan mobilized twenty thousand troops to relieve Sichuan and Shu, and afterward they fought hard at Bai River, Ju River, and Yuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan dispatched twenty thousand troops to relieve Sichuan, and they later fought hard at Bai River, Ju River, and Yuquan.

sentences.zh: 寶祐五年正月朔，以功拜參知政事。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the fifth year of Baoyou, for his merit he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fifth year of Baoyou he was appointed vice grand councilor for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 越七日，卒，贈少師，賻銀絹以五百計。

translations.literal: Seven days later he died. He was posthumously given the title of Junior Preceptor, and funeral gifts of silver and silk totaling five hundred were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later he died. He was posthumously made junior preceptor, and funeral gifts of silver and silk amounting to five hundred were granted.

sentences.zh: 淵有材略，迄濟事功，所至興學養士，然政尚嚴酷，好興羅織之獄，籍入豪橫，故時有“蜈蚣”之謠。

translations.literal: Yuan had talent and strategic ability and in the end accomplished useful work. Wherever he went he promoted schools and nurtured scholars, yet his government favored severity, he liked to fabricate prosecutions, and he confiscated the property of the overbearing, so at the time there was a saying about the "centipede."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had talent and strategic ability and in the end achieved real results. Wherever he served he promoted schools and nurtured scholars, yet his rule was harsh, he was fond of fabricated prosecutions, and he confiscated the property of the powerful, so people nicknamed him the "centipede."

sentences.zh: 其弟潛亦數諫止之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qian also repeatedly admonished him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qian also repeatedly urged him to stop.

sentences.zh: 所著《易解》及《退庵文集》、奏議。

translations.literal: His writings include the Explanations of the Changes and the Collected Works of the Retired Hermitage, as well as memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the 《Explanations of the Changes》 and the 《Collected Works of the Retired Hermitage》, along with various memorials.

sentences.zh: 餘玠，字義夫，蘄州人。

translations.literal: Yu Jie, styled Yifu, was a native of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jie, whose style was Yifu, was a native of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧落魄無行，喜功名，好大言。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he was dissolute and without proper conduct, fond of fame and given to grand talk.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; he was dissolute and ill-behaved, hungry for fame and fond of grand talk.

sentences.zh: 少為白鹿洞諸生，嚐攜客入茶肆，毆賣茶翁死，脫身走襄淮。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student at Bailudong. Once he brought guests into a teahouse, beat the tea seller to death, and escaped to Xianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied at Bailudong. Once he took guests into a teahouse, beat the tea seller to death, and fled to the Xiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 時趙葵為淮東製置使，玠作長短句上謁，葵壯之，留之幕中。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Kui was Huaidong Pacification Commissioner. Jie composed a ci poem and presented himself; Kui was impressed and kept him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Kui was Huaidong pacification commissioner. Jie composed a ci poem and presented himself; Kui was impressed and kept him on his staff.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以功補進義副尉，擢將作監主簿、權發遣招進軍，充製置司參議官，進工部郎官。

translations.literal: Before long, for merit he was given the supplementary post of Vice Commander of Advance Righteousness, promoted to Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, given provisional authority to dispatch the Recruitment Advance Army, appointed staff adviser of the Pacification Commission, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for merit he was given the supplementary post of vice commander of Advance Righteousness, promoted to registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, given provisional authority over the Recruitment Advance Army, made staff adviser of the pacification commission, and promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，與大元兵戰於汴城、河陰有功，授直華文閣、淮東提點刑獄兼知淮安州兼淮東製置司參謀官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi he fought the Great Yuan forces at Bian City and Heyin with merit, and was given the rank of Direct Attendant of the Hall of Chinese Glory, made Judicial Intendant of Huaidong while also governing Huai'an Prefecture and serving as staff adviser of the Huaidong Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiaxi he fought the Mongols at Bian City and Heyin with distinction and was made direct attendant of the Hall of Chinese Glory, judicial intendant of Huaidong while also governing Huai'an and serving as staff adviser of the Huaidong pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，玠提兵應援安豐，拜大理少卿，升製置副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou Jie led troops to relieve Anfeng, was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to Deputy Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou Jie led troops to relieve Anfeng, was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, and was promoted to deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進對：“必使國人上下事無不確實，然後華夏率孚，天人感格。

translations.literal: In an audience he said: "It is necessary to ensure that nothing done by those above and below in the state is untrue; only then will the Chinese lands be united in trust and Heaven and man be moved in response.
translations.idiomatic: In an audience he said, "The court must see to it that nothing done above or below in the realm is untrue; only then will the Chinese lands be united in trust and Heaven and man respond in harmony.

sentences.zh: ”又言：“今世胄之彥，場屋之士，田裏之豪，一或即戎，即指之為粗人，斥之為噲伍。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Today when scions of noble houses, examination graduates, or local magnates take up arms, they are at once called crude men and driven off as companions of Fan Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Today when sons of noble houses, examination graduates, or local magnates take up arms, they are at once called crude men and dismissed as no better than Fan Kuai's sort.

sentences.zh: 願陛下視文 武之士為一，勿令偏有所重，偏必至於激，文武交激，非國之福。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will regard civil and military men as one, and not allow partial favor to either side. Partiality necessarily leads to provocation; when civil and military provoke one another, it is not a blessing for the state.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to treat civil and military men as one body and not let either side be favored too heavily. Favoritism always provokes backlash; when civil and military provoke each other, it bodes ill for the realm.

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“卿人物議論皆不常，可獨當一面，卿宜少留，當有擢用。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your person and your discourse are both uncommon. You can hold a frontier on your own. You should stay a while longer; there will be promotion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You and your views are both out of the ordinary. You can hold a frontier on your own. Stay a while longer; promotion will come.

sentences.zh: ”乃授權兵部侍郎、四川宣諭 使，帝從容慰遣之。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Acting Vice Minister of War and Commissioner for Pacification and Instruction of Sichuan, and the emperor graciously comforted and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made acting vice minister of war and commissioner for pacification and instruction of Sichuan, and the emperor graciously comforted and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 玠亦自許當手挈全蜀還本朝，其功日月可冀。

translations.literal: Jie also promised himself that he would personally bring all of Shu back to the dynasty, and that his achievement could be expected day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Jie also promised himself that he would personally restore all of Shu to the dynasty, and that success was only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎、四川安撫製置使兼知重慶府兼四川總領兼夔路轉運使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Vice Minister of War, Sichuan Pacification and Pacification Commissioner while also governing Chongqing Prefecture, overall controller of Sichuan, and Transport Commissioner of Kuizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice minister of war, Sichuan pacification and pacification commissioner while also governing Chongqing, overall controller of Sichuan, and transport commissioner of Kuizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 自寶慶三年至淳祐二年，十六年間，凡授宣撫三人，製置使九人，副四人，或老或暫，或庸或貪，或慘或繆，或遙領而不至，或開隙而各謀，終無成績。

translations.literal: From the third year of Baoqing to the second year of Chunyou, across sixteen years, in all three Pacification Commissioners and nine Pacification Commissioners and four deputies were appointed—some old, some temporary, some mediocre, some greedy, some cruel, some mistaken, some holding posts in name but not arriving, some opening rifts and each pursuing his own plan—and in the end there was no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Baoqing to the second year of Chunyou, across sixteen years, three pacification commissioners, nine pacification commissioners, and four deputies were appointed—some aged, some temporary, some mediocre, some greedy, some cruel, some misguided, some holding posts in name but never arriving, some at odds and each pursuing his own plan—and in the end nothing was accomplished.

sentences.zh: 於是東、西 川無復統律，遺民鹹不聊生，監司、戎帥各專號令，擅辟守宰，蕩無紀綱，蜀日益壞。

translations.literal: Thus in Eastern and Western Chuan there was no longer unified discipline; the surviving people all could scarcely live; supervisory officials and military commanders each held sole authority over orders, arbitrarily appointed prefects and magistrates, and discipline was utterly lost, so Shu daily grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Chuan lost all unified command; the surviving people could barely live; supervisory officials and military commanders each issued orders on his own, appointed prefects and magistrates at will, and discipline collapsed, so Shu grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 及聞玠入蜀，人心粗定，始有安土之誌。

translations.literal: When they heard that Jie had entered Shu, hearts were roughly settled and people first had the will to settle on the land.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Jie had entered Shu, hearts steadied somewhat and people began to think of settling down.

sentences.zh: 玠大更敝政，遴選守 宰，築招賢之館於府之左，供張一如帥所居，下令曰：“集眾思，廣忠益，諸葛孔明所以用蜀也。

translations.literal: Jie greatly reformed corrupt policies, carefully selected prefects and magistrates, and built a Hall for Recruiting the Worthy to the left of the prefectural office, furnished exactly like the commander's residence. He issued an order saying: "Gather the thoughts of the multitude and broaden loyalty and benefit—this is how Zhuge Kongming used Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jie carried out sweeping reforms, carefully chose prefects and magistrates, and built a Hall for Recruiting the Worthy to the left of the prefectural office, furnished like the commander's own residence. He issued an order: "Gather the thoughts of many and broaden loyalty and benefit—this is how Zhuge Liang made use of Shu.

sentences.zh: 欲有謀以告我者，近則徑詣公府，遠則自言於郡，所在以禮遣之， 高爵重賞，朝廷不吝以報功，豪傑之士趨期立事，今其時矣。

translations.literal: Those who wish to offer counsel to me, if near may go directly to the public office; if far may report in their prefecture. Everywhere they shall be sent off with ceremony. High ranks and heavy rewards—the court will not be sparing in repaying merit. Heroes and outstanding men should hurry to establish achievements—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone with a plan to offer me, if nearby may come straight to this office, if far away may report through his prefecture. Everywhere they shall be sent off with full courtesy. High rank and rich reward—the court will not stint in repaying merit. Men of talent should hurry to accomplish something—now is the hour.

sentences.zh: ”士之至者，玠不厭禮接，鹹得其歡心，言有可用，隨其才而任之；

translations.literal: " When scholars arrived, Jie never tired of receiving them with ceremony; all won his favor. If their words were usable, he assigned them according to their talent;
translations.idiomatic: " When scholars came, Jie never tired of receiving them with full courtesy; all won his goodwill. If their advice was sound, he employed them according to their ability;

sentences.zh: 苟不可用，亦厚遺謝之。

translations.literal: if not usable, he also generously sent them off with gifts of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: if not, he still sent them away with generous gifts of thanks.

sentences.zh: 播州冉氏兄弟璡、璞，有文武才，隱居蠻中，前後閫帥辟召，堅不肯起，聞玠賢，相謂曰：“是可與語矣。

translations.literal: The Ran brothers Jin and Pu of Bozhou had civil and military talent and lived in seclusion among the barbarians. Successive frontier commanders had summoned them, but they firmly refused to rise. When they heard that Jie was worthy, they said to each other: "This is someone with whom one can speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Ran brothers Jin and Pu of Bozhou had civil and military talent and lived in seclusion among the tribes. Frontier commanders before and after had summoned them, but they steadfastly refused. When they heard that Jie was worthy, they said to each other, "Here is someone worth talking to.

sentences.zh: ”遂詣府上謁，玠素聞冉氏兄弟，刺入即出見之，與分 廷抗禮，賓館之奉，冉安之若素有，居數月，無所言。

translations.literal: " They then went to the prefectural office to pay their respects. Jie had long heard of the Ran brothers; as soon as their card was sent in he came out to meet them, shared the hall with them as equals, and lodged them in the guest quarters as if they had long been there. They stayed several months without saying anything.
translations.idiomatic: " They went to the prefectural office to pay their respects. Jie had long heard of the Ran brothers; as soon as their card arrived he came out to meet them, received them as equals in the hall, and lodged them in the guest quarters as if they were old friends. They stayed several months without saying a word.

sentences.zh: 玠將謝之，乃為設宴，玠親主之。

translations.literal: Jie was about to dismiss them with thanks when he set up a banquet and presided over it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was about to send them off with thanks when he gave a banquet and presided over it himself.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，坐客方紛紛競言所長，璡兄弟飲食而已。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, the guests were all eagerly competing to speak of their strengths, while the Ran brothers only ate and drank.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had warmed the guests, everyone else was eagerly airing his talents, but the Ran brothers only ate and drank.

sentences.zh: 玠以微言挑之，卒默然。

translations.literal: Jie tried to draw them out with subtle remarks, but in the end they remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Jie tried to draw them out with subtle remarks, but they remained silent to the end.

sentences.zh: 玠 曰：“是觀我待士之禮何如耳。

translations.literal: Jie said: "They are only observing how I treat scholars with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "They are only watching how I treat men of talent.

sentences.zh: ”明日更辟別館以處之，且日使人窺其所為。

translations.literal: " The next day he opened a separate lodge to house them and each day sent someone to observe what they were doing.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he set up a separate lodge for them and each day sent someone to watch what they were doing.

sentences.zh: 兄弟終日不言，惟對踞，以堊畫地為山川城池之形，起則漫去，如是又旬日，請見玠， 屏人曰：“某兄弟辱明公禮遇，思有以少裨益，非敢同眾人也。

translations.literal: The brothers spoke not all day but only sat facing each other, drawing mountains, rivers, and city forms on the ground with chalk, then rubbing them away when they rose. Thus for another ten days. They asked to see Jie and, dismissing attendants, said: "We brothers have been honored by your lordship's courteous treatment and wish to offer some small benefit—we do not presume to be like the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers spoke not all day but only sat facing each other, sketching mountains, rivers, and city layouts on the ground with chalk and rubbing them away when they rose. After another ten days of this they asked to see Jie and, sending attendants away, said, "We have been honored by your courtesy and wish to offer some small help—we do not presume to be like the others.

sentences.zh: 為今日西蜀之計，其在徙合州城乎？

translations.literal: For planning Western Shu today, is it not in moving Hezhou city?
translations.idiomatic: For the defense of western Shu today, is the answer not to move Hezhou?

sentences.zh: ”玠不覺躍起，執其手曰：“此玠誌也，但未得其所耳。

translations.literal: " Jie involuntarily leaped up, grasped their hands, and said: "This has been Jie's aim, but I had not found the place.
translations.idiomatic: " Jie leaped up without thinking, seized their hands, and said, "That has been my aim, but I had not found the place.

sentences.zh: ” 曰：“蜀口形勝之地莫若釣魚山，請徙諸此，若任得其人，積粟以守之，賢於十萬師遠矣，巴蜀不足守也。

translations.literal: " They said: "Of strategic places at the entrance to Shu none surpasses Diaoyu Mountain. Please move the city there. If the right man is appointed and grain is stored to hold it, that is better than a hundred thousand troops at a distance. Ba and Shu are not worth defending as they are.
translations.idiomatic: " They said, "Of strong points at the gateway to Shu none surpasses Diaoyu Mountain. Move the city there. If the right man is appointed and grain is stored to hold it, that is worth more than a hundred thousand troops far away. Ba and Shu as they stand are not worth defending.

sentences.zh: ”玠大喜曰：“玠固疑先生非淺士，先生之謀，玠不敢掠 以歸己。

translations.literal: " Jie was greatly pleased and said: "Jie had indeed suspected that you gentlemen were no shallow men. Your plan—Jie dare not claim it as his own.
translations.idiomatic: " Jie was overjoyed and said, "I had indeed suspected you were no ordinary men. Your plan—I dare not claim it as my own.

sentences.zh: ”遂不謀於眾，密以其謀聞於朝，請不次官之。

translations.literal: " He then did not consult the multitude but secretly reported their plan to the court and requested extraordinary promotion for them.
translations.idiomatic: " He then did not consult others but secretly reported their plan to the court and asked that they be given extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 詔以璡為承事郎、權發遣合州，璞為承務郎、權通判州事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jin as Gentleman for Attending Duty with temporary authority to oversee the relocation of He Prefecture, and Pu as Gentleman for Service with temporary authority as vice-prefect over prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Jin a Court Gentleman for Attending Duty with charge of moving He Prefecture and Pu a Court Gentleman for Service with acting authority as the prefecture's vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 徙城之事，悉以任之。

translations.literal: The entire matter of relocating the city was wholly entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: They were given full responsibility for the relocation.

sentences.zh: 命下，一府皆喧然同辭以 為不可。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, everyone in the prefectural office clamored together, all with one voice declaring it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Once the decree came down, the whole prefectural staff erupted in a chorus of opposition, insisting it was impossible.

sentences.zh: 玠怒曰：“城成則蜀賴以安，不成，玠獨坐之，諸君無預也。

translations.literal: Jie said angrily: "If the walls are completed, Shu will rely on them for security; if not, Jie alone will bear the penalty—you gentlemen need have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: Jie snapped, "Finish these forts and Sichuan is safe; fail, and only I answer for it—you need not worry.

sentences.zh: ”卒築青居、大獲、釣魚、雲頂、天生凡十餘城，皆因山為壘，棋布星分，為諸郡治所，屯兵 聚糧為必守計。

translations.literal: " In the end they built more than ten walled places including Qingju, Dahuo, Diaoyu, Yunding, and Tiansheng, all taking mountains as ramparts, arrayed like chess pieces and scattered stars, as seats of the various prefectures, stationing troops and gathering grain as a plan for certain defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they completed more than a dozen mountain fortresses—among them Qingju, Dahuo, Diaoyu, Yunding, and Tiansheng—cut into the hills and dotted across the map as prefectural seats, with garrisons and grain stores laid in for a defense that could be held.

sentences.zh: 且誅潰將以肅軍令。

translations.literal: Moreover they executed routed generals to stiffen military discipline.
translations.idiomatic: They also put fleeing commanders to death to restore discipline in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 又移金戎於大獲，以護蜀口。

translations.literal: They also shifted the Jin garrison to Dahuo to guard the mouth of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinzhou garrison was moved to Dahuo to cover the gateway into Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 移沔戎於青居，興戎先駐合州舊城，移守釣魚，共備內水。

translations.literal: They moved the Mian garrison to Qingju; the Xing garrison had first been stationed at He Prefecture's old city, then shifted to hold Diaoyu—all together to defend the inner waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The Mianzhou troops went to Qingju; the Xingzhou force, first posted at old He Prefecture city, was reassigned to Diaoyu; together they secured the inner river routes.

sentences.zh: 移利戎於雲頂，以備外水。

translations.literal: They moved the Li garrison to Yunding to guard against the outer waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The Lizhou garrison was redeployed to Yunding to watch the outer water lines.

sentences.zh: 於是如臂使 指，氣勢聯絡。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was like an arm directing its fingers, their momentum linked together.
translations.idiomatic: The line now moved as one limb, every post in concert.

sentences.zh: 又屬嘉定俞興開屯田於成都，蜀以富實。

translations.literal: He also assigned Yu Xing of Jiading to open military colonies at Chengdu, and Shu thereby grew rich and full.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yu Xing of Jiading in charge of opening government farms around Chengdu, and Sichuan grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，玠率諸將巡邊，直搗興元，大元兵與之大戰。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year, Jie led the generals on a border inspection, striking straight at Xingyuan; Great Yuan troops fought a great battle with him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, Jie took his generals on a frontier tour, drove straight into Xingyuan, and clashed in a major battle with the Yuan armies.

sentences.zh: 十二年，又大戰於嘉定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, again a great battle at Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later came another major fight at Jiading.

sentences.zh: 初，利司都統 王夔素殘悍，號“王夜叉”，恃功驕恣，桀驁不受節度，所至劫掠，每得富家，穴箕加頸，四面然箕，謂之“蟆蝕月”，以弓弦係鼻下，高懸於格，謂之“錯係喉 ”，縛人兩股，以木交壓，謂之“幹榨油”，以至用醋灌鼻、惡水灌耳口等，毒虐非一，以脅取金帛，稍不遂意，即死其手，蜀人患苦之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Kui of the Li circuit, chief commander, had always been cruel and fierce, styled "King Yaksha." Relying on merit he was arrogant and willful, defiant and insubordinate, plundering wherever he went. Whenever he seized a wealthy household, he would bore a winnowing basket, place it over the neck, and set fire on all four sides—calling this "toad gnawing the moon." He would tie a bowstring under the nose and hang the victim high on a frame—calling this "throat wrongly bound." He would bind a man's two thighs and press them with crossed timbers—calling this "dry-pressing oil"—and on to pouring vinegar into the nose and foul water into the ears and mouth, with cruelties not of one kind alone, to extort gold and silk. If slightly displeased, the victim died at his hand; the people of Shu suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: From the start, Wang Kui, chief commander of the Lizhou circuit, had been savage and brutal, known as "King Yaksha." He traded on his victories for arrogance, refused all discipline, and looted wherever he marched. When he cornered a rich family he might force a winnowing basket over the neck and set it alight on every side—a torture he called "the toad devouring the moon." He would loop a bowstring under the nose and hoist the victim on a frame—"throat wrongly trussed." He would bind a man's legs and crush them with crossed beams—"dry-pressing for oil"—and go on to pour vinegar up the nose and filthy water into the ears and mouth. His tortures were endless, all to wring out gold and silk; the slightest displeasure meant death, and the people of Shu lived in misery.

sentences.zh: 且悉斂部將倅馬以自入， 將戰，乃高其估賣與之。

translations.literal: Moreover he collected all his subordinate officers' and deputies' horses for his own intake; only when battle was imminent would he mark up the price and sell them back.
translations.idiomatic: He also seized his subordinates' mounts for himself and only on the eve of battle sold them back at inflated prices.

sentences.zh: 朝廷雖知其不法，在遠不能詰也。

translations.literal: Although the court knew of his lawlessness, being far away it could not investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew he broke the law but could not reach him in that distant post to hold him to account.

sentences.zh: 大帥處分，少不嗛其意，則百計撓之，使不得有所為。

translations.literal: When the supreme commander issued disposition, if it slightly failed to satisfy his intent, he would devise a hundred schemes to obstruct it, so that [the commander] could accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the commander-in-chief gave orders he disliked, he sabotaged them by every trick until nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 玠至嘉定，夔帥所部兵迎謁，才贏弱二百人。

translations.literal: When Jie arrived at Jiading, Kui led his troops to greet him in audience—but only a lean two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie reached Jiading, Kui came out to receive him with a paltry, undersized band of two hundred.

sentences.zh: 玠 曰：“久聞都統兵精，今疲敝若此，殊不稱所望。

translations.literal: Jie said: "Long have I heard that the commander's troops are elite; now they are worn and weak like this—quite unlike what was hoped.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "I have long heard your troops were first-rate; to see them so worn and few falls far short of what I expected.

sentences.zh: ”夔對曰：“夔兵非不精，所以不敢即見者，恐驚從人耳。

translations.literal: " Kui replied: "Kui's troops are not unelite; the reason I did not present them at once is that I feared startling your attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Kui answered, "My men are not unfit; I held them back lest they startle your escort.

sentences.zh: ”頃之，班聲如雷，江水如沸，聲止，圓陣即合，旗幟 精明，器械森然，沙上之人彌望若林立，無一人敢亂行者。

translations.literal: " In a moment drums sounded like thunder and the river like boiling; when the sound ceased, circular formations at once closed, banners bright and weapons dense. On the sandbank people stretched as far as the eye could see, standing like a forest—no one dared walk out of order.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later drums rolled like thunder and the river seemed to boil. When the noise stopped, ring formations snapped shut, banners sharp and arms glittering. The shore was packed shoulder to shoulder; not a man stepped out of line.

sentences.zh: 舟中皆戰掉失色，而玠自若也。

translations.literal: Those in the boats all trembled and turned pale, while Jie remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the boats shook and went white, but Jie was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 徐命吏班賞有差。

translations.literal: Slowly he ordered clerks to distribute rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly had his staff hand out rewards by rank.

sentences.zh: 夔退謂人曰：“儒者中乃有此人！”

translations.literal: Kui withdrew and said to others: "Among scholars there is such a man!
translations.idiomatic: Kui withdrew and said to his men, "Among scholars there is such a man as this!

sentences.zh: 玠久 欲誅夔，獨患其握重兵居外，恐輕動危蜀，謀於親將楊成，成曰：“夔在蜀久，所部兵精，前時大帥，夔皆勢出其右，意不止此也。

translations.literal: Jie had long wished to execute Kui, but only feared that with heavy troops stationed outside, a rash move might endanger Shu. He consulted his trusted general Yang Cheng. Cheng said: "Kui has been in Shu a long time and his troops are elite. In former times the great commanders were all outranked by Kui in power; his ambitions do not stop here.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had long wanted Kui dead but feared that with so many troops under him in the field, a rash move could shake all of Sichuan. He took counsel with his trusted officer Yang Cheng, who said, "Kui has been in Shu for years with crack troops. Past commanders were all outshone by him—his ambitions do not end here.

sentences.zh: 視侍郎為文臣，必不肯甘心從 令，今縱弗誅，養成其勢。

translations.literal: Seeing the Vice Minister as a civil official, he will surely be unwilling to submit willingly to orders. If now you do not execute him, you will nurture his power.
translations.idiomatic: He sees you as a civilian minister and will never willingly obey. Spare him now and you only feed his strength.

sentences.zh: 後一舉足，西蜀危矣。

translations.literal: Later, with one move of the foot, western Shu will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: One step more and all western Shu is at risk.

sentences.zh: ”玠曰：“我欲誅之久矣，獨患其黨與眾，未發耳。

translations.literal: " Jie said: "I have wished to kill him a long time, but only feared his faction was numerous and had not yet acted.
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "I have wanted him dead for years, but his following is large and I have not yet struck.

sentences.zh: ”成曰：“侍郎以夔在蜀久，有威名，孰與吳氏？

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "The Vice Minister considers that Kui has been long in Shu and has prestige—compared with the Wu family, how is he?
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "You think Kui's long service has made him formidable—but how does he compare with the Wu clan?

sentences.zh: 夔固弗若 也。

translations.literal: Kui is certainly not their equal.
translations.idiomatic: He is nothing beside them.

sentences.zh: 夫吳氏當中興危難之時，能百戰以保蜀，傳之四世，恩威益張，根本益固，蜀人知有吳氏而不知有朝廷。

translations.literal: When the Wu family stood in the peril of the dynasty's revival, they could fight a hundred battles to preserve Shu, passing through four generations; favor and awe grew ever greater, their roots ever firmer, and the people of Shu knew the Wu family and did not know the court.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's darkest hour the Wu clan fought a hundred battles to hold Shu, held power for four generations, and grew so rooted that the people knew Wu and scarcely knew the throne.

sentences.zh: 一旦曦為叛逆，諸將誅之如取孤豚。

translations.literal: Once Xi rebelled, the generals executed him like taking a lone pig.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi rebelled, his officers cut him down as easily as catching a stray pig.

sentences.zh: 況夔無吳氏之功， 而有曦之逆心，恃豨突之勇，敢慢法度，縱兵殘民，奴視同列，非有吳氏得人之固也。

translations.literal: As for Kui, he has none of the Wu family's achievements but has Xi's rebellious heart, relying on the courage of a rampaging boar, daring to slight the law, letting troops harm the people and treating peers as slaves—he does not have the Wu family's solid hold on men's loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Kui has none of the Wu merit yet shares Xi's rebellious bent. He trusts only brute daring, flouts the law, lets his men prey on the people, and treats fellow officers like servants—he lacks the Wu hold on men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 今誅之，一夫力耳，待其發而取之，難矣。

translations.literal: To kill him now is the strength of one man; wait until he rises and take him—it will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now and it is one man's work; wait until he moves and it will be far harder.

sentences.zh: ”玠意遂決，夜召夔計事，潛以成 代領其眾，夔才離營，而新將已單騎入矣，將士皆愕眙相顧，不知所為。

translations.literal: " Jie's mind was then decided. At night he summoned Kui to discuss affairs and secretly had Cheng take command of his troops. Kui had only left camp when the new commander had already entered alone on horseback; officers and soldiers all stared in shock at one another, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Jie made up his mind. That night he called Kui in on business while secretly putting Cheng in command of his troops. Kui had barely left camp when the new commander rode in alone; the men gaped at one another, stunned.

sentences.zh: 成以帥指譬曉之，遂相率拜賀，夔至，斬之。

translations.literal: Cheng explained the commander's intent to them; they thereupon bowed in succession to congratulate. When Kui arrived, he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng explained the commander's orders; the troops bowed in turn. When Kui appeared, they cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 成因察其所與為惡者數人，稍稍以法誅之。

translations.literal: Cheng then identified several men who had done evil with him and gradually executed them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng picked out several of Kui's accomplices and put them to death one by one under the law.

sentences.zh: 乃 薦成為文州刺史。

translations.literal: Then he recommended Cheng as prefect of Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Cheng for appointment as prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 玠自入蜀，進華文閣待制，賜金帶，權兵部尚書，進徽猷閣學士，升大使，又進龍圖閣學士、端明殿學士，及召，拜資政殿學士，恩例視執政。

translations.literal: From the time Jie entered Shu he was advanced to Attendant at the Huawen Pavilion, granted a gold belt, given acting authority as Minister of War, advanced to Academician of the Huixian Pavilion, raised to Grand Commissioner, again advanced to Academician of the Longtu and Duanming halls, and when summoned was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall, with favors equal to those of a chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After Jie entered Sichuan he rose to Attendant at the Huawen Pavilion, received a gold belt and acting rank as Minister of War, became Academician of the Huixian Pavilion and then Grand Commissioner, later Academician of the Longtu and Duanming halls, and on recall was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall with privileges matching a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，帝輟朝，特贈五官。

translations.literal: At his death the emperor halted court; he was specially posthumously granted five ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor suspended court and posthumously raised him five ranks.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史陳大方言奪職。

translations.literal: Because Supervising Censor Chen Dafang spoke, his offices were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On the memorial of Supervising Censor Chen Dafang his offices were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 六年，復之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later they were restored.

sentences.zh: 玠之治蜀也，任都統張實治軍旅，安撫王惟忠治財賦，監簿朱文炳接賓客，皆有常度。

translations.literal: In Jie's governing of Shu, he charged Chief Commander Zhang Shi with military affairs, Pacification Commissioner Wang Weizhong with revenue, and Registrar Zhu Wenbing with receiving guests—each had fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: In governing Sichuan, Jie put Chief Commander Zhang Shi in charge of the army, Pacification Commissioner Wang Weizhong in charge of finances, and Registrar Zhu Wenbing in charge of guests—each with clear rules.

sentences.zh: 至於修學養士，輕徭以寬民力，薄征以通商賈。

translations.literal: As for cultivating learning and nurturing scholars, light corvée to broaden the people's strength, and thin levies to open commerce.
translations.idiomatic: He fostered schools and scholars, eased labor service to lighten the people's burden, and cut taxes to encourage trade.

sentences.zh: 蜀既富實，乃罷京湖之餉；

translations.literal: Shu having grown rich and full, he then ended the grain shipments from Jing and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sichuan was prosperous he ended grain shipments from the Jing-Hu region.

sentences.zh: 邊關無警，又撤東南之戍。

translations.literal: With no alarm on the borders, he again withdrew the garrisons of the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier was quiet he pulled back southeastern garrisons as well.

sentences.zh: 自寶慶以來，蜀閫未有能及之者。

translations.literal: Since the Baoqing era there had been no commander of the Sichuan frontier who could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Baoqing reign no Sichuan commander had matched him.

sentences.zh: 惜其遽以太平自詫，進蜀錦蜀箋，過於文飾。

translations.literal: It is a pity that he too quickly boasted of peace to himself, presenting Shu brocade and Shu paper with excessive ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he too soon congratulated himself on peace, sending up Sichuan brocade and stationery with excessive display.

sentences.zh: 久假便宜之權，不顧嫌疑，昧於勇退，遂來讒賊之口；

translations.literal: Having long held extraordinary discretionary power, he did not heed suspicion, was blind to bold withdrawal, and thus slanderers found their opening;
translations.idiomatic: He held extraordinary powers too long, ignored the suspicion this aroused, and failed to step down in time—so calumny found its way in;

sentences.zh: 而 又置機捕官，雖足以廉得事情，然寄耳目於群小，虛實相半，故人多懷疑懼。

translations.literal: and again he set up secret arrest officials; although this was enough to investigate affairs cleanly, yet he entrusted eyes and ears to petty men, truth and falsehood half and half, so many people harbored doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: and he set up secret investigators. Though they could expose wrongdoing, he also relied on petty informers, so truth and rumor mingled and many lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 至於世安拒命，玠威名頓挫，齎誌以沒。

translations.literal: As for Yao Shi'an's refusal of orders, Jie's prestige suddenly collapsed, and he died carrying his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Shi'an defied his orders, Jie's authority collapsed overnight, and he died with his aims unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 有子曰如孫，取“當如孫仲謀”之義，遭論改 師忠，曆大理寺丞，為賈似道所殺。

translations.literal: He had a son named Rusun, taking the sense of "one ought to be like Sun Zhongmou"; because of criticism his name was changed to Shizhong. He served as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was killed by Jia Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Rusun—from "one should be like Sun Zhongmou"—later renamed Shizhong after criticism. He rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and was killed by Jia Sidao.

sentences.zh: 汪立信，澈從孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Lixin was a collateral descendant of Che.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lixin was a distant nephew of Wang Che.

sentences.zh: 立信曾大父智從澈宣諭湖北，道六安，愛其山水，因居焉。

translations.literal: Lixin's great-grandfather Zhi followed Che on a mission to pacify Hubei; passing through Lu'an he loved its mountains and waters and therefore settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin's great-grandfather Zhi had followed Che on a mission to pacify Hubei; passing through Lu'an he fell in love with the landscape and settled there.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，立信獻策 招安慶劇賊胡興、劉文亮等，借補承信郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou, Lixin presented a plan to pacify the fierce bandits Hu Xing, Liu Wenliang, and others of Anqing, and was provisionally appointed Gentleman for Trust.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou, Lixin proposed a plan to pacify the Anqing bandits Hu Xing, Liu Wenliang, and others, and received provisional appointment as Gentleman for Trust.

sentences.zh: 六年，登進士第，理宗見立信狀貌雄偉，顧侍臣曰：“此閫帥才也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he passed the jinshi examination; Lizong saw Lixin's imposing appearance and turned to his attendants, saying: "This is material for a frontier commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he passed the jinshi examination. Lizong saw his imposing bearing and told his attendants, "Here is a man fit to command the frontier.

sentences.zh: ”授烏江主簿，辟沿江製幕。

translations.literal: " He was appointed registrar of Wujiang and recruited to the Yangtze defense staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was made registrar of Wujiang and recruited to the Yangtze defense headquarters.

sentences.zh: 知桐城縣，未上，辟荊 湖製司幹辦、通判建康府。

translations.literal: He was made magistrate of Tongcheng but had not taken up the post when he was recruited as staff officer of the Jing-Hu commission and vice-prefect of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Tongcheng but before taking office was recruited as staff officer on the Jing-Hu commission and vice-prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 荊湖製置趙葵辟充策應使司及本司參議官。

translations.literal: Jing-Hu Commissioner Zhao Kui recruited him as planning officer of the campaign staff and as councillor of the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jing-Hu Commissioner Zhao Kui made him planning officer on the campaign staff and a commission councillor.

sentences.zh: 葵去而馬光祖代之，立信是時猶在府也。

translations.literal: When Kui departed Ma Guangzu replaced him; Lixin was still in the office at that time.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui left, Ma Guangzu replaced him; Lixin remained in the office.

sentences.zh: 鄂州圍解，賈似道既罔上要功，惡閫外 之臣與己分功，乃行打算法於諸路，欲以軍興時支散官物為罪，擊去之。

translations.literal: When the siege of E Prefecture was lifted, Jia Sidao, having concealed the emperor's merit for himself, hated frontier officials who might share credit with him and therefore imposed an audit law on the various circuits, wishing to charge them with official goods disbursed during the military emergency and drive them out.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege of Ezhou was lifted, Jia Sidao, having claimed the credit for himself, resented frontier officers who might share it and imposed an audit on every circuit, seeking to charge them with wartime disbursements and remove them.

sentences.zh: 光祖與葵素有隙，且欲迎合似道，被旨即召吏稽勾簿書，卒不能得其疵。

translations.literal: Guangzu had long borne a grudge against Kui and moreover wished to please Sidao; receiving the order he at once summoned clerks to audit the account books, but in the end could not find a flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu had long disliked Kui and wanted to please Sidao. Ordered to audit the books, he could find no fault.

sentences.zh: 乃以開慶二年正月 望夕，張燈宴設錢三萬緡為葵放散官物聞於朝。

translations.literal: He therefore reported to court that on the Lantern Festival of the first month of the second year of Kaiqing, Kui had set out lamps and a feast, disbursing thirty thousand strings of cash as official goods.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported that on the Lantern Festival of the first month, Kaiqing year 2, Kui had held a feast with lamps and disbursed thirty thousand strings of cash as official funds.

sentences.zh: 立信力爭之，謂不可，且曰：“方艱難時，趙公蒞事勤勞，而公以非理捃拾之。

translations.literal: Lixin argued forcefully that it could not be done, and moreover said: "In hard times Zhao served diligently, yet you pick on him unreasonably.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin protested that this was wrong and said, "In hard times Zhao served diligently, yet you hound him without cause.

sentences.zh: 公一旦去此，後來者復效公所為，可 乎？

translations.literal: Once you leave this post, those who come after will again imitate what you have done—can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Leave this post and your successors will do the same—is that acceptable?

sentences.zh: ”光祖怒曰：“吾不才不能為度外事，知奉朝命而已。

translations.literal: " Guangzu said angrily: "I am without talent and cannot do extraordinary affairs; I know only to follow the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu snapped, "I am no genius for extraordinary measures; I only follow the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 君他日處此，勉為之。

translations.literal: When you one day hold this post, exert yourself at it.
translations.idiomatic: One day you will sit here—do your best then.

sentences.zh: ”立信曰：“使某不為則已，果為之，必不效公所為也。

translations.literal: " Lixin said: "If I do not act, that is one thing; if I truly act, I will certainly not imitate what you have done.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin said, "If I do nothing, so be it; if I act, I will not copy you.

sentences.zh: ”光祖益怒，議不行，立 信遂投劾去。

translations.literal: " Guangzu grew angrier; the plan did not proceed, and Lixin thereupon submitted his resignation and left.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu grew angrier still. The case went nowhere, and Lixin resigned.

sentences.zh: 初，立信通判江陵府，葵製置荊湖，嚐以公事劾立信，及在沿江府，亦謀議寡諧，立信於葵蓋未嚐有一日之歡也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lixin was vice-prefect of Jiangling Prefecture, Kui as Jing-Hu commissioner had once impeached him on official business; when he was on the Yangtze staff their plans rarely agreed—Lixin and Kui had never had a single day of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as vice-prefect of Jiangling, he had been impeached by Kui on official grounds; on the Yangtze staff their views rarely aligned—Lixin and Kui had never been on good terms for a single day.

sentences.zh: 擢京西提舉常平，改知 昭信軍、權淮東提刑。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Jingxi grain intendant, changed to military commissioner of Zhaoxin, and given acting authority as Huai-East judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jingxi grain intendant, made military commissioner of Zhaoxin, and given acting authority as Huai-East judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，差知池州、提舉江東常平、權知常州、浙西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding he was assigned to know Chizhou, to direct Jiangdong grain transport, with acting authority over Changzhou and as Zhexi judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingding year 1 he was assigned to Chizhou, put in charge of Jiangdong grain transport, given acting authority over Changzhou, and made Zhexi judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，即嘉興治所講行荒政。

translations.literal: The next winter he at once carried out famine relief at the Jiaxing headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he ran famine relief from the Jiaxing headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋改知江州，充沿江製置副使、節製蘄黃興 國軍馬、提舉饒州南康兵甲，升江西安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to know Jiang Prefecture, made vice commissioner of Yangtze defense, given command of troops at Qi, Huang, and Xingguo, and raised to Jiangxi pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Jiangzhou, vice Yangtze defense commissioner, commander of Qi, Huang, and Xingguo troops, and Jiangxi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乞祠祿，差知鎮江，尋充湖南安撫使、知潭州。

translations.literal: He requested a stipend post, was assigned to know Zhenjiang, and soon made Hunan pacification commissioner and prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a stipend post, was sent to Zhenjiang, and soon made Hunan pacification commissioner and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 至官，供帳之物悉置官庫，所積錢連歲代納潭民夏稅，貧無告者予錢 粟，病者加藥餌，雨雪旱潦軍民皆有給。

translations.literal: On taking office he placed all supplies and furnishings in the official treasury; the money accumulated over successive years he used to pay the summer tax of the people of Tan for them. To those poor with no one to appeal to he gave money and grain; to the sick he added medicine. In snow, rain, flood, or drought both army and people received relief.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he put all official furnishings in the treasury; for years he used stored funds to pay Tan people's summer tax. He gave grain and cash to the destitute, medicine to the sick, and relief to soldiers and civilians in flood, drought, snow, or rain.

sentences.zh: 興學校，士習為變。

translations.literal: He raised schools, and scholarly practice was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: He founded schools and changed the tone of local scholarship.

sentences.zh: 以潭為湖湘重鎮，創威敵軍，所募精銳數千人，後來者果賴其用。

translations.literal: Because Tan was a key post of Hunan and Hubei, he created the Weidi Army and recruited several thousand elite troops; those who came after indeed relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou was the strategic heart of Hunan and Hubei; he created the Weidi Army and recruited several thousand crack troops whom later commanders would rely on.

sentences.zh: 權兵部尚書、荊湖安撫製置、知江陵 府。

translations.literal: He was given acting authority as Minister of War, Jing-Hu pacification commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He received acting rank as Minister of War, Jing-Hu pacification commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽被圍危急，立信上疏“請益安陸府屯兵，凡邊戍皆不宜抽減，黃州守臣陳奕素蓄異志，朝廷宜防之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiangyang was besieged in critical peril; Lixin memorialized: "Please increase the garrison troops of Anlu Prefecture. All frontier garrisons should not be reduced. Chen Yi, the defending official of Huang Prefecture, has long harbored disloyal intent; the court should guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang was in desperate siege. Lixin memorialized, "Increase the garrison at Anlu. Do not strip the border posts. Chen Yi at Huangzhou has long shown disloyal intent—the court must watch him.

sentences.zh: ”乃移書似道，謂：“今天下之勢十去 八九，而君臣宴安不以為虞。

translations.literal: " He then sent a letter to Sidao, saying: "Today the realm's situation is nine-tenths gone, yet ruler and ministers feast in ease and take no thought of it.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Sidao, "Nine parts in ten of the realm are already lost, yet court and emperor feast as if nothing were wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫天之不假易也，從古以然，此誠上下交修以迓續天命之幾，重惜分陰以趨事赴工之日也。

translations.literal: That Heaven does not grant ease has been so from antiquity; this is truly the moment when above and below should together reform to meet Heaven's continuing mandate, and cherish every hour to hurry affairs and rush to work.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has never granted ease lightly—that has been true since antiquity. This is the hour when court and country must reform together to keep Heaven's mandate and treasure every moment for real work.

sentences.zh: 而乃酣歌深宮，嘯傲湖山，玩歲悽日，緩急 倒施，卿士師師非度，百姓鬱怨非上，以求當天心，俯遂民物，拱揖指揮而折衝萬里者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Yet they sing deep in the palace, whistle proudly over lakes and hills, play away the years in sorrow, reverse urgency and leisure, officials and scholars act without measure, and the people's resentment does not reach above—to seek to accord with Heaven's heart, bend to the people's things, and with folded hands command and repel enemies ten thousand li away: is that not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Instead they carouse in the inner palace, idle on lakes and hills, let the years slip by, put leisure before urgency, let officials run wild and the people's anger never reach the throne—how can folded hands at a distance turn back enemies ten thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 為今日之計者，其策有三。

translations.literal: For planning today there are three policies.
translations.idiomatic: For the present crisis there are three policies.

sentences.zh: 夫內郡何事乎多兵，宜盡出之江幹， 以實外禦。

translations.literal: What need have inner prefectures for many troops? They should all be sent out to the river front to strengthen outer defense.
translations.idiomatic: Inner circuits do not need large garrisons; send every man to the river line to hold the outer frontier.

sentences.zh: 算兵帳見兵可七十餘萬人，老弱柔脆，十分汰二，為選兵五十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Counting the military rolls, visible troops number more than seven hundred thousand; of the old, weak, and tender, cut two in ten, selecting more than five hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The rolls show over seven hundred thousand men on paper; cull the old and weak by two in ten and you have more than five hundred thousand fit soldiers.

sentences.zh: 而沿江之守，則不過七千里，若距百里而屯，屯有守將，十屯為府，府有總督，其 尤要害處，輒參倍其兵。

translations.literal: Along the river the defense would be no more than seven thousand li; if posted every hundred li, each post would have a defending general; ten posts would make a fu, each fu a governor-general; at the most critical points, double the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze line is barely seven thousand li; post a commander every hundred li, group ten posts into a command, place a governor over each, and double the garrison at the weakest points.

sentences.zh: 無事則泛舟長淮，往來遊徼，有事則東西齊奮，戰守並用。

translations.literal: In peace they would sail the long Huai, coming and going on patrol; in crisis east and west would strike together, using attack and defense alike.
translations.idiomatic: In peace they would patrol the Huai by boat; in war they would strike east and west together, fighting and holding as one.

sentences.zh: 刁鬥相聞，饋餉不絕，互相應援，以為聯絡之固。

translations.literal: Watch-fires would be heard from post to post, supplies would not cease, and mutual support would make the linkage firm.
