translations.idiomatic: Watch-fires would link post to post, supplies would flow without break, and mutual relief would bind the line.

sentences.zh: 選宗室親王、忠良有幹用大 臣，立為統製，分東西二府，以蒞任得其人，率然之勢，此上策也。

translations.literal: Select imperial clansmen, princes, and great ministers loyal and capable, establish them as overall commanders, divide east and west into two commands, place the right men in charge—with such a formed momentum, this is the upper policy.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint imperial princes and proven ministers as supreme commanders, split the line into eastern and western commands, and put the right men in charge—that is the best policy.

sentences.zh: 久拘聘使，無益於我，徒使敵得以為辭，請禮而歸之，許輸歲幣以緩師期，不二三年，邊遽稍 休，藩垣稍固，生兵日增，可戰可守，此中策也。

translations.literal: Long detained envoys are of no benefit to us and only let the enemy make excuses; please treat them with courtesy and send them home, allow annual tribute to ease the enemy's timetable—in no more than two or three years the border alarm will gradually ease, the defensive screen gradually firm, live troops daily increase, able to fight and able to hold: this is the middle policy.
translations.idiomatic: Holding envoys gains nothing and only gives the enemy a pretext; return them with courtesy, pay annual tribute to buy time—in two or three years the frontier may quiet, the defenses stiffen, and fresh troops accumulate until we can fight and hold. That is the middle policy.

sentences.zh: 二策果不得行，則天敗我也，若銜璧輿櫬之禮，則請備以俟。

translations.literal: If the two policies truly cannot be carried out, then Heaven has defeated us; as for the ritual of jade disk and coffin, please prepare and wait."
translations.idiomatic: If neither policy can be adopted, Heaven has already condemned us; as for the rites of surrender with jade and coffin, let us prepare for that."

sentences.zh: ”似道得書大怒，抵之地，詬曰：“瞎賊狂言敢爾。

translations.literal: " Sidao, receiving the letter, was greatly enraged, dashed it to the ground, and cursed: "Blind traitor—dare you speak so wildly!
translations.idiomatic: Sidao read the letter, flew into a rage, threw it down, and shouted, "Blind rebel—how dare you rant like this!

sentences.zh: ”蓋以立信目微眇雲。

translations.literal: " This was because Lixin's eyes were slightly dim.
translations.idiomatic: He said this because Lixin's eyes were slightly clouded.

sentences.zh: 尋中以危法廢斥之。

translations.literal: Soon he was charged under a grave law and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was charged under a serious statute and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳十年，大元兵大舉伐宋，似道督諸軍出次江上，以立信為端明殿學士、沿江製置使、江淮招討使，俾就 建康府庫募兵以援江上諸郡。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun the Great Yuan troops launched a great campaign against Song; Sidao supervised the armies and encamped on the river, appointing Lixin Academician of the Duanming Hall, Yangtze defense commissioner, and Huai-Jiang campaign commissioner, ordering him to recruit troops at Jiankang's treasury to aid the upper-river prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianchun year 10 the Yuan launched a full invasion. Sidao took command on the river and made Lixin Academician of the Duanming Hall, Yangtze defense commissioner, and Huai-Jiang campaign commissioner, with orders to raise troops from Jiankang's stores to relieve the upper-river prefectures.

sentences.zh: 立信受詔不辭，即日上道，以妻子讬愛將金明，執其手曰：“我不負國家，爾亦必不負我。

translations.literal: Lixin received the order without declining and that same day set out on the road. He entrusted his wife and children to his beloved general Jin Ming, grasped his hand, and said: "I will not fail the state; you too must not fail me.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin accepted without hesitation and left the same day. He entrusted his wife and children to his trusted officer Jin Ming, took his hand, and said, "I will not fail the country; you must not fail me.

sentences.zh: ”遂行。

translations.literal: " He then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he went.

sentences.zh: 與似道遇蕪湖，似道拊立信背哭 曰：“不用公言，以至於此。

translations.literal: Meeting Sidao at Wuhu, Sidao patted Lixin's back and wept, saying: "I did not use your words, and it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuhu he met Sidao, who clapped him on the back and wept, "I would not heed you—and see where we are."

sentences.zh: ”立信曰：“平章、平章，瞎賊今日更說一句不得。

translations.literal: " Lixin said: "Minister, Minister—the blind bandit cannot utter one more word today.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin said, "Minister, Minister—you blind bandit will not get to say another word today."

sentences.zh: ”似道問立信何向？

translations.literal: " Sidao asked Lixin where he was headed.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao asked where he was going.

sentences.zh: 曰：“今江南無一寸乾淨地，某去尋一片趙家地上死，第要死 得分明爾。

translations.literal: He said: "Today not one inch of land south of the Yangtze is clean. I am going to find a patch of Zhao family ground on which to die—only that I die clearly."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "There is not a clean inch left in the south. I am going to find a scrap of Zhao soil to die on—so long as I die with honor."

sentences.zh: ”既至，則建康守兵悉潰，而四面皆北軍。

translations.literal: " When he arrived, Jiankang's defending troops had all scattered, and on every side were northern troops.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Jiankang's garrison had melted away and northern armies surrounded him on every side.

sentences.zh: 立信知事不可成，歎曰：“吾生為宋臣，死為宋鬼，終為國一死，但徒死無益耳，以此負國。

translations.literal: Lixin knew affairs could not succeed and sighed: "I was born a Song subject; I shall die a Song ghost. In the end I will die once for the state—but a useless death profits nothing, and by this I fail the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin saw that nothing could be saved and sighed, "Born a Song subject, I shall die a Song ghost. I will die for the country—but a pointless death helps no one, and that is how I fail it.

sentences.zh: ”率所部數千人 至高郵，欲控引淮漢以為後圖。

translations.literal: " He led several thousand men of his command to Gaoyou, intending to hold the Huai and Han rivers for later designs.
translations.idiomatic: He led several thousand men to Gaoyou, hoping to hold the Huai and Han for a later campaign.

sentences.zh: 已而聞似道師潰蕪湖，江漢守臣皆望風降遁。

translations.literal: Shortly after he heard that Sidao's army had collapsed at Wuhu and that defending officials of the Yangtze and Han had all fled and surrendered at the first rumor.
translations.idiomatic: Then he heard that Sidao's army had been routed at Wuhu and that officials along the Yangtze and Han were surrendering or fleeing without a fight.

sentences.zh: 立信歎曰：“吾今日猶得死於宋土也。

translations.literal: Lixin sighed: "Today I can still die on Song soil.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin sighed, "At least I can still die on Song soil."

sentences.zh: ”乃置酒召賓佐與訣，手為表起居三宮，與從子書，屬以家事。

translations.literal: " He then set out wine, summoned his staff to bid farewell, and personally drafted memorials of regard for the Three Palaces; he wrote his nephew and entrusted him with family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He called his staff to a farewell feast, wrote memorials to the Three Palaces with his own hand, and sent a letter to his nephew entrusting family matters.

sentences.zh: 夜分起步庭中，慷慨悲歌，握拳撫案者三，以是失聲，三日扼吭而卒。

translations.literal: At midnight he rose and paced the courtyard, singing boldly in grief; three times he clenched his fist and struck the table—thereby losing his voice, and on the third day he died with a strangled throat.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he paced the courtyard, singing in grief; three times he struck the table with his fist until his voice broke, and on the third day he died by strangulation.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫致仕，遺表聞，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He had retired as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; when his final memorial was reported, he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He had retired as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; when his final memorial reached the court, he was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 大元丞相伯顏入建康，金明以其家人免，或惡立信於伯顏，以其二策及其死告，且請戮其孥，伯顏歎息久之，曰：“宋有是人，有是言哉！

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Bayan of the Great Yuan entered Jiankang; Jin Ming was spared through his family. Someone bore malice toward Lixin before Bayan and reported his two policy memorials and manner of death, also asking to execute his children. Bayan sighed long and said: "The Song had such a man and such words!
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Chancellor Bayan of the Great Yuan entered Jiankang, Jin Ming was spared on account of his family. Someone slandered Lixin to Bayan, reporting his two policy memorials and how he had died, and asked that his sons be put to death. Bayan sighed and said, "The Song had such a man—and such counsel!

sentences.zh: 使果用，我安得至此。

translations.literal: Had they truly been used, how could I have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: If they had truly been followed, how would I have come this far?

sentences.zh: ”命求其家厚恤之，曰：“忠臣之家也。

translations.literal: " He ordered Lixin's family sought out and generously comforted, saying: "The household of a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Lixin's family found and richly compensated, saying, "This is the house of a loyal minister."

sentences.zh: ”金明以立信之喪歸葬丹陽。

translations.literal: " Jin Ming brought Lixin's coffin home for burial at Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Ming returned Lixin's coffin for burial at Danyang.

sentences.zh: 立信子麟，內書寫機宜文字，在建康不肯從眾降，崎嶇走閩以死。

translations.literal: Lixin's son Lin, Inner Palace Document Officer for confidential dispatches, at Jiankang would not follow the crowd in surrender; by hard paths he fled to Fujian and died.
translations.idiomatic: Lixin's son Lin, a confidential secretary in the inner palace, refused to surrender with the others at Jiankang, fled overland to Fujian, and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 初，立信之未仕也，家窶甚。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Lixin entered office, his family was very poor.
translations.idiomatic: Before Lixin entered office, his family was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 會歲大侵，吳淵守鎮江，命為粥以食流民，使其客黃應炎主之。

translations.literal: It happened that a year of great famine came; Wu Yuan guarded Zhenjiang and ordered porridge made to feed the displaced, putting his client Huang Yingyan in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe famine Wu Yuan, as prefect of Zhenjiang, set up gruel kitchens for refugees and put his client Huang Yingyan in charge.

sentences.zh: 應炎一見立信，與語，心知其非常人，言於淵，淵大奇之，禮以上 客，凡共張服禦視應炎為有加，應炎甚怏怏。

translations.literal: At first sight Yingyan spoke with Lixin and in his heart knew him an extraordinary man; he told Yuan, and Yuan was greatly struck, treating him as an honored guest. In all shared provisions, dress, and transport he looked better than Yingyan, and Yingyan was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyan met Lixin once and knew at once he was no ordinary man; he told Yuan, who was astonished and received him as an honored guest, lavishing provision, clothing, and transport on him beyond what he gave Yingyan, who grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 淵解之曰：“此君，吾地位人也，但遭時不同耳。

translations.literal: Yuan explained: "This gentleman is a man of my own stature, only his time differs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reassured him: "This man is my equal in rank—only fate has not favored him yet.

sentences.zh: 君之識度誌業，皆非其倫也，盍少下之。

translations.literal: Your breadth of vision, resolve, and career are none of his class—why not humble yourself a little?"
translations.idiomatic: Your vision and ambition are beyond his class—you might show a little deference."

sentences.zh: ”是年，試江東轉運司，明 年登第，後其踐曆略如淵而卒死於難，人謂淵能知人雲。

translations.literal: " That year he tested at the Jiangdong Transport Commission; the next year he passed the examinations. Later his career roughly followed Yuan's, yet he died in calamity—people said Yuan could judge men.
translations.idiomatic: That year he sat for the Jiangdong transport exam; the next year he passed the jinshi. His career later loosely mirrored Yuan's, yet he perished in the fall—people said Yuan had known a man when he saw one.

sentences.zh: 向士璧，字君玉，常州人。

translations.literal: Xiang Shibi, styled Junyu, was a man of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shibi, styled Junyu, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 負才氣，精悍甚自好，紹定五年進士，累通判平江府，以臣僚言 罷。

translations.literal: He relied on talent and spirit, was keen and very proud of himself. In the fifth year of Shaoding he became a jinshi; he repeatedly served as vice-prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture and was dismissed on officials' memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and combative, he was sharp-witted and fiercely proud. He passed the jinshi in Shaoding year 5, served repeatedly as vice-prefect of Pingjiang, and was dismissed after memorials from colleagues.

sentences.zh: 起為淮西製置司參議官，又以監察御史胡泓言罷。

translations.literal: He was reappointed a planning officer of the Huai-West Pacification Commission, then again dismissed on the memorial of Supervising Censor Hu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as planning officer on the Huai-West Pacification staff, then dismissed again on a memorial from Supervising Censor Hu Hong.

sentences.zh: 起知高郵軍，製置使丘崇又論罷。

translations.literal: He was raised to administer Gaoyou Army; Pacification Commissioner Qiu Chong again memorialized for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Gaoyou, then ousted again by Pacification Commissioner Qiu Chong.

sentences.zh: 起知安慶府、知黃州，遷淮西提點刑獄兼知黃州，加直寶章閣，仍舊職，奉 鴻禧祠。

translations.literal: He was raised to administer Anqing Prefecture and Huang Prefecture, promoted to Huai-West judicial intendant while also administering Huang, granted direct appointment to the Baozhang Pavilion while retaining his post, and received offerings at the Hongxi Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Anqing and Huang, then Huai-West judicial intendant and prefect of Huang, was granted direct access to the Baozhang Pavilion, and received stipends at the Hongxi Shrine.

sentences.zh: 特授將作監、京湖製置參議官，進直煥章閣、湖北安撫副使兼知峽州，兼歸峽施黔、南平軍、紹慶府鎮撫使，遷太府少卿、大理卿，進直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: Specially appointed Director of Palace Construction and planning officer of the Jing-Hu Pacification Commission, he advanced to direct appointment to the Huanzhang Pavilion, Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hubei and administrator of Xia Prefecture, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Gui-Xia, Shi, Qian, Nanping Army, and Shaoqing Prefecture, then promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and advanced to direct appointment to the Longtu Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially made Director of Palace Construction and Jing-Hu planning officer, then Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hubei and prefect of Xia, concurrently commissioner over Gui-Xia, Shi, Qian, Nanping, and Shaoqing, then Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse and chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and gained direct access to the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 合州告 急，製置使馬光祖命士璧赴援，數立奇功。

translations.literal: Hezhou reported urgent peril; Pacification Commissioner Ma Guangzu ordered Shibi to go to its relief, and he repeatedly won signal merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhou was in desperate straits, Pacification Commissioner Ma Guangzu sent Shibi to relieve it, and he won repeated signal victories.

sentences.zh: 帝亦語群臣曰：“士璧不待朝命，進師歸州，且捐家貲百萬以供軍費，其誌足嘉。

translations.literal: The emperor also told the assembled ministers: "Shibi did not wait for court orders but advanced his army to Guizhou and moreover contributed a million in family wealth to supply the army—his resolve is worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers, "Shibi did not wait for orders before marching to Guizhou, and he gave a million in family funds to the army—his spirit deserves praise."

sentences.zh: ”進秘閣修撰、樞密副都承旨，仍舊 職。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Secretariat Compiler and Deputy Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, while retaining his posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Compiler and Deputy Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，涪州危，又命士璧往援，北兵夾江為營，長數十里，阻舟師不能進至浮橋。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing, Fuzhou was in peril and Shibi was again ordered to its relief. Northern troops made camps on both banks of the river for several tens of li, blocking the fleet from reaching the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiqing year 1, when Fuzhou was threatened, Shibi was sent again. Yuan forces camped for miles along both banks of the river and blocked his fleet from the pontoon bridge.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷自揚州移賈似道以樞密使宣撫六路，進駐峽州，檄士 璧以軍事付呂文德，士璧不從，以計斷橋奏捷，具言方略。

translations.literal: At that time the court moved Jia Sidao from Yangzhou as Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner to pacify the six circuits and advanced to encamp at Xia Prefecture, ordering Shibi to hand military affairs to Lü Wende; Shibi refused, used a stratagem to cut the bridge, and reported victory while setting forth his plan in full.
translations.idiomatic: The court had moved Jia Sidao from Yangzhou as Military Affairs Commissioner to pacify six circuits and posted him at Xia; Sidao ordered Shibi to hand command to Lü Wende. Shibi refused, cut the bridge by stratagem, reported victory, and laid out his plan in full.

sentences.zh: 未幾，文德亦以捷聞。

translations.literal: Before long Wende also reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wende reported victory as well.

sentences.zh: 士璧還峽州，方懷傾奪之疑，尋辟為宣撫司參議官，遷湖南安撫副使兼知潭州，兼 京西、湖南北路宣撫司參議官，加右文殿修撰，尋授權兵部侍郎、湖南安撫使兼知潭州。

translations.literal: Shibi returned to Xia Prefecture. Just as he harbored suspicion of being stripped of merit, he was soon appointed planning officer of the Pacification Commission, promoted to Vice Pacification Commissioner of Hunan and administrator of Tan Prefecture, concurrently planning officer of the Jingxi and Hunan North Route Pacification Commission, granted the post of Right Culture Hall Compiler, then appointed acting Vice Minister of War, Hunan Pacification Commissioner, and administrator of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Xia he feared his credit would be stolen; he was soon made pacification planning officer, then Hunan Vice Pacification Commissioner and prefect of Tan, planning officer on the Jingxi and northern Hunan staff, Right Culture Hall compiler, and finally acting Vice Minister of War with Hunan command and the Tan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 頃之，升湖南製置副使。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was promoted to Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 大元將兀良哈<角┦>兵自交阯北 還，前鋒至城下，攻圍急，士璧極力守禦，聞後隊且至，遣王輔佑率五百人往覘之，以易正大監其軍，遇於南嶽市，一戰有功，潭州圍遂解。

translations.literal: The Mongol general Uriyangqadai, returning north from Jiaozhi with his troops, had his vanguard reach the walls and press the siege hard. Shibi defended with all his strength. Hearing that the rear columns were approaching, he sent Wang Fuyou with five hundred men to reconnoiter, with Yi Zhengda supervising the army. They met them at Nanyue market, fought one battle with merit, and the siege of Tanzhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol general Uriyangqadai was marching north from Jiaozhi; his vanguard reached the walls and pressed the siege fiercely. Shibi defended with all his strength. When he heard the rear guard was coming, he sent Wang Fuyou with five hundred men to scout, with Yi Zhengda supervising the force. They met at Nanyue market, won a sharp fight, and the siege of Tanzhou was lifted.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜金帶，令服 係，進兵部侍郎兼轉運使，餘依舊職。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was granted a gold belt and ordered to wear it tied on, promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrently Transport Commissioner, his other posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court he received a gold belt and orders to wear it, was promoted to Vice Minister of War and transport commissioner, and kept his other posts.

sentences.zh: 似道入相，疾其功，非獨不加賞，反諷監察御史陳寅、侍御史孫附鳳一再劾罷之，送漳州居住。

translations.literal: When Sidao entered the chancellorship he resented Shibi's merit; not only did he withhold reward, he had Supervising Censor Chen Yin and Attending Censor Sun Fufeng impeach him repeatedly until he was dismissed and sent to live at Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sidao became chief councilor he envied Shibi's success; he not only withheld reward but had Censor Chen Yin and Attending Censor Sun Fufeng impeach him until he was exiled to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又稽守城時所用 金穀，逮至行部責償。

translations.literal: He also audited the gold and grain used during the siege and pursued Shibi to his tour of office to make repayment.
translations.idiomatic: He also audited the gold and grain spent in the defense and pursued Shibi on his inspection tour to force repayment.

sentences.zh: 幕屬方元善者，極意逢迎似道意，士璧坐是死，復拘其妻妾而征之。

translations.literal: A staff member, Fang Yuanshan, curried Sidao's favor to the utmost; Shibi died on account of this, and his wives and concubines were seized and taxed.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Fang Yuanshan went to great lengths to please Sidao; Shibi died as a result, and his wives and concubines were seized and made to pay.

sentences.zh: 其後元善改知吉水縣，俄歸得狂疾，常呼士璧。

translations.literal: Later Yuanshan was transferred to administer Jishui County; before long he returned home with a mad illness and constantly cried out for Shibi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuanshan was made magistrate of Jishui; he soon came home insane and kept calling for Shibi.

sentences.zh: 時輔佑亦遠謫，及文天祥 起兵召輔佑於謫所，則死矣。

translations.literal: At that time Fuyou was also exiled far away; when Wen Tianxiang raised troops and summoned Fuyou from exile, he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyou was also in distant exile; when Wen Tianxiang raised the banner and summoned him, he was already dead.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年三月，詔追復元官，仍還從官恩數，立廟潭州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Deyou an edict restored his former rank and returned the privileges of his former office; a temple was erected at Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Deyou year 1 an edict restored his former rank and privileges, and a temple was raised at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，太府卿柳嶽乞錄用其子孫，詔從之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Grand Storehouse Minister Liu Yue asked that his sons and grandsons be recorded for office; the edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the first month, Grand Storehouse Minister Liu Yue asked that his sons and grandsons be enrolled for office, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 胡 穎，字叔獻，潭州湘潭人。

translations.literal: Hu Ying, styled Shuxian, was a man of Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying, styled Shuxian, was from Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父琮，娶趙方弟雍之女，二子，長曰顯，有拳勇，以材武入官，數有戰功，事見《趙範傳》。

translations.literal: His father Cong married a daughter of Zhao Fang's younger brother Yong; there were two sons. The elder, Xian, had boxing courage and entered office through martial talent, winning repeated battle merit—his affairs are recorded in the 《Biography of Zhao Fan》.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cong married a daughter of Zhao Fang's younger brother Yong; they had two sons. The elder, Xian, was a fierce fighter who entered office by martial merit and won repeated victories—his story appears in the 《Biography of Zhao Fan》.

sentences.zh: 穎自幼風神秀異，機警不常，趙氏諸舅以其 類己，每加賞鑒。

translations.literal: From childhood Ying's bearing and spirit were outstanding and unusual, his wit unsettled; the Zhao uncles on his mother's side, finding him like themselves, always praised and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Ying was striking in bearing and uncannily quick-witted; his Zhao uncles on his mother's side, seeing themselves in him, always singled him out for praise.

sentences.zh: 成童即能背誦諸經，中童子科，復從兄學弓馬，母不許，曰：“汝家世儒業，不可復爾也”。

translations.literal: As a youth he could recite the classics from memory, passed the child examination, then studied archery and horsemanship with his cousin; his mother would not allow it, saying: "Your family for generations has pursued Confucian learning—you must not do so again."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he could recite the classics from memory, passed the child examination, then tried to study archery and horsemanship with his cousin; his mother forbade it, saying, "Our family has been Confucian for generations—you must not take that path again."

sentences.zh: 遂感勵苦學，尤長於《春秋》。

translations.literal: He was moved to study hard and excelled especially in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into study and became especially accomplished in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 紹定三 年，範討李全，檄穎入幕，穎常微服行諸營，察眾誌向，歸必三鼓。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoding, Fang campaigned against Li Quan and summoned Ying to his staff; Ying often went about the camps in plain dress to observe the troops' morale, always returning at the third watch.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding year 3, Zhao Fang campaigned against Li Quan and took Ying onto his staff; Ying often walked the camps in disguise to read the men's mood, always returning at the third watch.

sentences.zh: 後全敗，遣穎獻俘於朝，以賞補官。

translations.literal: After Quan was defeated he sent Ying to present captives at court and received office by reward.
translations.idiomatic: After Quan's defeat he sent Ying to present captives at court and received office by reward.

sentences.zh: 五年，登進士第，即授京秩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he passed the jinshi examination and was immediately given capital rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he passed the jinshi and was immediately given a capital appointment.

sentences.zh: 曆官知平江府兼浙西提點刑 獄，移湖南兼提舉常平，即家置司。

translations.literal: In successive posts he administered Pingjiang Prefecture while concurrently serving as Zhexi judicial intendant, then moved to Hunan while concurrently supervising the Ever-Normal Granary, establishing his office at home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Pingjiang and Zhexi judicial intendant, then moved to Hunan as Ever-Normal intendant, establishing his office at home.

sentences.zh: 性不喜邪佞，尤惡言神異，所至毀淫祠數千區，以正風俗。

translations.literal: By nature he disliked flattery and especially hated talk of the supernatural; wherever he went he destroyed thousands of illicit shrines to rectify custom.
translations.idiomatic: He detested flattery and especially loathed talk of spirits; wherever he served he tore down thousands of illicit shrines to set custom right.

sentences.zh: 衡州有靈祠，吏民夙所畏事，穎撤之，作來諗堂奉母居之，嚐語道州 教授楊允恭曰：“吾夜必瞑坐此室，察影響，鹹無有。

translations.literal: Heng Prefecture had a numinous shrine that officials and people had long feared and served; Ying demolished it and built the Laishen Hall to house his mother. He once told Yang Yungong, professor at Daozhou: "Each night I must sit in this room with eyes closed, observing shadows and sounds—and there are none.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou had a spirit shrine officials and commoners had long feared; Ying tore it down and built the Laishen Hall for his mother. He told Daozhou professor Yang Yungong, "Every night I sit in this room with my eyes closed, watching for omens—and there are none.

sentences.zh: ”允恭對曰：“以為無則無矣，從而察之。

translations.literal: " Yungong replied: "To think there is none is already to have none; yet if you go on observing,
translations.idiomatic: " Yungong answered, "To decide there is nothing is already enough; but if you keep watching,

sentences.zh: 則是又疑其有也。

translations.literal: then you are again suspecting that there is.
translations.idiomatic: you are suspecting again that something might be there."

sentences.zh: ”穎甚善其言。

translations.literal: " Ying greatly approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ying greatly approved of this.

sentences.zh: 以樞密都承旨為廣 東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: As Deputy Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs he became Guangdong Pacification Commissioner and Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Deputy Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs he became Guangdong Pacification Commissioner and Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 潮州僧寺有大蛇能驚動人，前後仕於潮者皆信奉之。

translations.literal: A Buddhist temple in Chaozhou had a great serpent that could startle people; successive officials who served in Chaozhou all revered it.
translations.idiomatic: A Chaozhou monastery kept a great serpent that terrified people, and every prefect before Ying had worshipped it.

sentences.zh: 前守去，州人心疑焉，以為未嚐詣也；

translations.literal: When the previous prefect left, the people of the prefecture were suspicious, thinking he had never paid a visit;
translations.idiomatic: When the last prefect left, the people suspected him because he had never paid his respects;

sentences.zh: 已而旱，鹹咎守不敬蛇神故致此，後守不得已詣焉，已而 蛇蜿蜒而出，守大驚得疾，旋卒。

translations.literal: then drought came and all blamed the prefect for disrespect to the serpent god and causing this; the next prefect had no choice but to go, and then the serpent writhed out— the prefect was greatly frightened, took ill, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: then drought struck and they blamed his disrespect to the serpent god; the next prefect had to go, the serpent slithered out, and he was so terrified he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 穎至廣州，聞其事，檄潮州令僧舁蛇至，至則其大如柱而黑色，載以闌檻，穎令之曰：“爾有神靈當三日見變怪，過三日則汝無神 矣。

translations.literal: When Ying reached Guangzhou and heard of the affair, he ordered the Chaozhou magistrate to have the monks carry the serpent to him. When it arrived it was as large as a pillar and black; it was loaded on a railing cart. Ying commanded it: "If you have spiritual power you should show wonders within three days; after three days you have no spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou Ying heard the story and ordered Chaozhou to send the serpent carried by monks. It was pillar-thick and black, hauled on a cart. Ying told it, "If you are divine, show a wonder in three days; after three days you are nothing but a snake.

sentences.zh: ”既及期，蠢然猶眾蛇耳，遂殺之，毀其寺，並罪僧。

translations.literal: " When the term was up it was sluggishly like any serpent; he had it killed, destroyed the temple, and punished the monks.
translations.idiomatic: " When the three days passed it was only an ordinary serpent; he had it killed, razed the temple, and punished the monks.

sentences.zh: 移節廣西，尋遷京湖總領財賦。

translations.literal: He moved his commission to Guangxi, then was transferred to overall fiscal intendant of Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his commission to Guangxi, then became overall fiscal intendant of Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳間卒，贈四官。

translations.literal: He died in the Xianchun period and was posthumously granted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He died during Xianchun and was posthumously promoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 穎為人正直剛果，博學強記，吐辭成 文，書判下筆千言，援據經史，切當事情，倉卒之際，對偶皆精，讀者驚歎。

translations.literal: Ying was upright and resolute in person, learned with a strong memory; when he spoke it came out as prose. In written judgments he wrote a thousand words at a stroke, citing classics and histories to fit the matter; even in haste his parallel prose was refined, and readers marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was upright, forceful, and learned, with a formidable memory; he spoke in finished prose and drafted judgments of a thousand words at a stroke, citing classics and histories to the point. Even in haste his parallel prose was polished, and readers marveled.

sentences.zh: 臨政善斷，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: In governing he judged well and did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In office he judged decisively and did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 在浙西，榮王府十二人行劫，穎悉斬之。

translations.literal: In Zhexi, twelve men of the Rong princely establishment committed robbery; Ying executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhexi twelve men of the Rong princely establishment committed robbery; Ying executed them all.

sentences.zh: 一日輪對，理宗曰：“ 聞卿好殺。

translations.literal: One day in turn at audience Lizong said: "We hear you love killing.
translations.idiomatic: At court one day Lizong said, "We hear you love killing."

sentences.zh: ”意在浙獄，穎曰：“臣不敢屈太祖之法以負陛下，非嗜殺也。

translations.literal: " He meant the Zhexi cases; Ying said: "Your servant dares not bend Taizu's law to fail Your Majesty—it is not that I love killing.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant the Zhexi cases. Ying said, "I dare not bend Taizu's law to fail Your Majesty—I do not love killing.

sentences.zh: ”帝為之默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor fell silent on this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said nothing more.

sentences.zh: 冷應澄，字公定，隆興分寧人。

translations.literal: Leng Yingcheng, styled Gongding, was a man of Fenning in Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Yingcheng, styled Gongding, was from Fenning in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年進士，調廬陵主簿，即以廉能著。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoqing he became a jinshi and was posted as chief clerk of Luling; he was at once noted for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Baoqing year 1 and was posted chief clerk of Luling, where he was immediately known for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 有事台府者，必曰：“願下廬陵清主簿。

translations.literal: When there were matters for the provincial commission, people always said: "Let it go down to the honest chief clerk of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a case went to the provincial commission, people would say, "Send it to the honest chief clerk of Luling.

sentences.zh: ”尤為楊長孺所識拔。

translations.literal: " Yang Changru especially recognized and promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Changru especially recognized and promoted him.

sentences.zh: 調靜江府司錄參軍，治獄平恕，轉運使範應鈴列薦於朝。

translations.literal: He was transferred to recorder of Jingjiang Prefecture, judged cases with fairness and mercy, and Transport Commissioner Fan Yingling listed him for recommendation to court.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to recorder of Jingjiang, he judged with fairness and mercy, and Transport Commissioner Fan Yingling recommended him to court.

sentences.zh: 知萬載縣，大修學舍，招俊秀治其業，旌其通經飭行者以勸。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Wanzai he greatly repaired the school, recruited talented youths to pursue their studies, and honored those who mastered the classics and kept proper conduct to encourage others.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Wanzai he rebuilt the school, recruited promising students, and honored those who mastered the classics and lived uprightly to encourage the county.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，棄孩滿道，乃下令恣民收養，所棄父母不得復問，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In a lean year abandoned children filled the roads; he then ordered that the people might adopt freely—the abandoning parents might not reclaim them—and very many lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year abandoned children filled the roads; he decreed that anyone might adopt freely and that abandoning parents could not reclaim them, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 葉夢得列其行事，風厲餘邑。

translations.literal: Ye Mengde listed his deeds, and his rigor inspired the neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengde commended his work, and his rigor inspired neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 通判道州。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 入監行在榷貨務，遷登聞鼓檢院。—

translations.literal: He entered service at the Capital Monopoly Office of the traveling court, then was promoted to the Petition Inspection Office of the Court of Imperial Supplications.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Capital Monopoly Office at the traveling court, then was promoted to the Petition Inspection Office.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，奉使督餉江上，還，知德慶府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding he was sent on mission to supervise grain on the river; on his return he administered Deqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingding year 1 he was sent to supervise river grain; on his return he became prefect of Deqing.

sentences.zh: 前守政不立，縱豪吏漁獵，峒獠遂大為變，逼城六十里而營。

translations.literal: The previous prefect did not establish policy but let powerful clerks plunder; the cave tribes then rose in great revolt and encamped sixty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect had been weak and let powerful clerks prey on the people; the cave tribes rose in revolt and pitched camp sixty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 應澄未入境，馳檄諭之曰：“汝等不獲已至此，新太守且 上，轉禍為福，一機也。

translations.literal: Before Yingcheng had entered the border he sent a flying dispatch to instruct them: "You have been driven to this against your will. The new prefect is about to arrive—turn misfortune to fortune; this is your one chance.
translations.idiomatic: Before he crossed the border he sent a fast dispatch: "You have been driven to this. A new prefect is coming—turn misfortune to fortune; this is your chance.

sentences.zh: 脅從影附，亦宜早計去就，不然不免矣。

translations.literal: Those who followed under coercion should also plan early whether to stay or go; otherwise you cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Those who followed under duress should decide early to stay or leave; otherwise you cannot escape."

sentences.zh: ”獠感悟欲自歸，惑謀主不果，眾稍引去，應澄知其勢解，即厲士馬，出不意一鼓擒之，縱遣歸 農，猶千餘人，乃請諸監司，歸郡之避難留幕府者，誅豪吏之激禍者。

translations.literal: " The tribes were moved and wished to surrender themselves, but the scheming leaders would not allow it; the masses gradually drew away. Yingcheng knew their force was dissolving, then roused soldiers and horses, struck unexpectedly in one drumbeat and captured them, released more than a thousand to return to farming, then asked the various supervisory offices to return to the prefecture those who had taken refuge in the staff, and execute the powerful clerks who had provoked the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " The tribes were moved and wanted to submit, but ringleaders blocked them and the crowd began to disperse. Seeing their strength break, Yingcheng rallied troops, struck by surprise, captured the leaders, sent more than a thousand back to their fields, then asked the supervisory offices to return refugees from his staff and execute the clerks who had provoked the revolt.

sentences.zh: 初經略雷宜中意應澄必以濟師來請，及是歎服，亟上其事，薦應澄可大用。

translations.literal: Earlier Pacification Commissioner Lei Yizhong had been certain Yingcheng would ask for troops to relieve the crisis; now he admired him, quickly reported the affair upward, and recommended that Yingcheng was fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Lei Yizhong had been sure Yingcheng would ask for troops; now he admired him, reported at once, and recommended him for high office.

sentences.zh: 屬縣 租賦，諉道阻久不至郡，應澄為之期曰：“首輸者與減分，末至則償所減。

translations.literal: Subordinate counties' tax grain, pleading that roads were blocked, had long failed to reach the prefecture; Yingcheng set a term for them: "Whoever pays first receives a reduction in quota; whoever pays last must repay what was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate counties had long withheld tax grain, claiming blocked roads; Yingcheng set terms: "Whoever pays first gets a quota reduction; whoever pays last must repay what was reduced.

sentences.zh: ”民惟恐後，不一月訖事。

translations.literal: " The people feared to be last and within one month the matter was finished.
translations.idiomatic: " The people raced to pay, and within a month all was collected.

sentences.zh: 凡諸綱官廩稍軍券，前政積不得者悉補還之，上下欣附。

translations.literal: As for all grain for transport posts, military rations, and army certificates that previous administrations had failed to deliver, he made full repayment, and high and low rejoiced in attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He repaid all transport grain, military rations, and army certificates that previous administrations had withheld, and officials and people alike rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 應澄 亦極力摩撫，與為簡便。

translations.literal: Yingcheng also strove to comfort and soothe, simplifying matters for them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingcheng worked hard to comfort the people and simplified procedures.

sentences.zh: 期年報政，奏罷抑配鹽法及乞用楮券折銀綱等五事，以紓民力，詔就升本道提舉常平兼轉運使，俾行其說。

translations.literal: At the end of a year he reported achievements, memorialized to abolish the forced salt quota and asked to use paper notes to meet silver transport quotas, among five measures to ease the people's burden; an edict promoted him on the spot to intendant of the Ever-Normal Granary and transport commissioner for the circuit, so that he might carry out his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he reported success, memorialized to end forced salt quotas and to use paper notes for silver transport, among five measures to ease the people; the court promoted him to Ever-Normal intendant and transport commissioner for the circuit so he could enact his plan.

sentences.zh: 首劾守令貪橫不法十餘人，列郡 肅然。

translations.literal: First he impeached more than ten prefects and magistrates who were greedy, overbearing, and lawless, and the prefectures were all awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: He first impeached more than ten greedy and lawless prefects and magistrates, and the circuit fell silent.

sentences.zh: 最聞，加直秘閣。

translations.literal: When his excellence was reported he was granted direct appointment to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his excellence was reported he gained direct access to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時經略使陳宗禮入為參知政事，帝問誰可代卿者，宗禮以應澄對，旋召為都官郎官，未行，就升直寶章閣、知廣州，主管廣南東路經略安撫 司公事、馬步軍都總管，領漕、庾如故。

translations.literal: At that time Pacification Commissioner Chen Zongli entered office as Vice Grand Councilor; the emperor asked who could replace him, and Zongli answered with Yingcheng. He was soon summoned as Director of the Ministry of Justice; before he set out he was promoted on the spot to direct appointment to the Baozhang Pavilion and administrator of Guangzhou, in charge of the Eastern Guangnan Pacification Commission, overall commander of infantry and cavalry, retaining grain and fiscal duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Pacification Commissioner Chen Zongli became Vice Grand Councilor, the emperor asked who could replace him; Zongli named Yingcheng. He was summoned as Director of the Ministry of Justice; before he departed he was promoted to direct access to the Baozhang Pavilion and prefect of Guangzhou, in charge of Eastern Guangnan pacification and overall commander of infantry and cavalry, retaining grain and fiscal duties.

sentences.zh: 五司叢劇，應澄即分時理務，不擾不倦，常曰：“治官事當如家事，惜官物當如己物。

translations.literal: The five offices were tangled and heavy; Yingcheng at once divided the hours to handle affairs, neither disturbing nor wearying, and often said: "In governing official business one should treat it like household affairs; in cherishing official goods one should treat them like one's own.
translations.idiomatic: Five offices pressed on him at once; Yingcheng divided the day among them without fuss or fatigue, and often said, "Run public business as you would your household; guard public goods as your own.

sentences.zh: 方今國計內虛，邊聲外 震，吾等受上厚恩，安得清談自高以誤世。

translations.literal: Today the state's revenue is hollow within and alarms shake the borders without—we who receive such deep grace from above, how can we hold lofty empty talk and mislead the age?
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty within and alarms shake the borders without—we who have received such grace from above, how can we indulge in lofty talk and fail the age?

sentences.zh: 陶士行、卞望之吾師也。

translations.literal: Tao Shixing and Bian Wangzhi are my teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shixing [Tao Kan] and Bian Wangzhi were my models.

sentences.zh: ”自聞襄、樊受圍，日繕器械，裕財粟，以備倉卒，後卒賴其用，屢平大寇，未嚐輕殺，笞杖以 降，亦加審慎，至其臨事輒斷，雖勢要不為撓奪。

translations.literal: " After hearing Xiangyang and Fancheng were besieged, he daily repaired weapons and amassed wealth and grain to prepare for sudden emergencies; troops later relied on these stores and he repeatedly pacified great bandits. He never lightly killed; even for those reduced to beating with the stick he was very cautious. When affairs came before him he decided at once, and even powerful men could not sway him.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he learned that Xiangyang and Fancheng were under siege, he repaired arms every day and stockpiled money and grain against sudden need. The army later depended on these reserves, and he put down major raids again and again. He never took life lightly; even when offenders were punished only with the rod he proceeded with care. In office he decided matters on the spot, and not even the well-connected could deflect him.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at his home.

sentences.zh: 豳字西士，少從錢文子學，登嘉泰二年進士第，授安吉州教授。

translations.literal: Bin, style name Xishi, in youth studied under Qian Wenzi, passed the jinshi in the second year of Jiatai, and was appointed professor of Anji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Xishi, a nephew of Cao Shuyuan, studied in his youth under Qian Wenzi, took his jinshi in Jiatai 2 (1202), and was made professor at Anji.

sentences.zh: 調重慶府司法參軍，郡守度正欲薦之，豳辭曰：“章司錄母老，請先之。

translations.literal: He was transferred as judicial adjutant of Chongqing prefecture. The prefect Du Zheng wished to recommend him; Bin declined, saying, "Registrar Zhang's mother is elderly--please put him first.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to serve as judicial adjutant in Chongqing, he was about to be recommended by the prefect, Du Zheng, when Bin declined: "Registrar Zhang has an aged mother; recommend him first.

sentences.zh: ”正敬 歎。

translations.literal: " Zheng admired him and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: " Du Zheng marveled and sighed with respect.

sentences.zh: 改知建昌縣，復故尚書李常山房，建齋舍以處諸生。

translations.literal: He was changed to magistrate of Jianchang county, restored the former residence of the former Minister Li Changshan, and built study halls to house students.
translations.idiomatic: Made magistrate of Jianchang, he restored the old residence of the former Minister Li and built dormitories for his students.

sentences.zh: 擢秘書丞兼倉部郎官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretary of the Secretariat and concurrently vice director of the Palace Provision Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to secretary of the Secretariat and concurrent vice director in the Palace Provision Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為浙西提舉常平，麵陳和糴折納之敝，建虎丘書院以祀尹焞。

translations.literal: Sent out as Zhexi intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries, he stated in person the abuses of harmonized purchase and commuted payments, and built Tiger Hill Academy to honor Yin Chun.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhexi intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries, he laid before the court the abuses of state grain purchases and commuted levies, and founded Tiger Hill Academy in memory of Yin Chun.

sentences.zh: 移浙東提點刑獄，寒 食放囚歸祀其先，囚感泣如期至。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhedong judicial intendant, on Cold Food Festival he released prisoners to return and sacrifice to their ancestors; the prisoners wept in gratitude and returned on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Zhedong as judicial intendant, he released prisoners at Cold Food to worship their ancestors; moved to tears, they came back on the day promised.

sentences.zh: 召為左司諫，與王萬、郭磊卿、徐清叟俱負直聲，當時號“嘉熙四諫”。

translations.literal: Summoned as remonstrator of the Left Bureau, together with Wang Wan, Guo Leiqing, and Xu Qingsou he all bore a reputation for integrity; at the time they were styled the "Four Remonstrators of Jiaxi."
translations.idiomatic: Called to the Left Bureau as remonstrator, he joined Wang Wan, Guo Leiqing, and Xu Qingsou in a reputation for blunt integrity; contemporaries called them the Four Remonstrators of Jiaxi.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：“立太子、厚倫紀，以弭火災”。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying, "Establish the crown prince and strengthen human relations to quell fire disasters."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he urged the throne to name an heir and shore up the bonds of kinship in order to still the fires that plagued the capital.

sentences.zh: 又論餘天錫、 李鳴復之過，迕旨，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: He again criticized the faults of Yu Tianxi and Li Mingfu, went against the imperial intent, and was transferred to director of imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the misconduct of Yu Tianxi and Li Mingfu; crossing the court, he was shifted to the post of director of imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，不拜，疏七上，進古詩以寓規正。

translations.literal: Advanced to vice minister of rites, he did not accept the appointment, memorialized seven times, and presented ancient-style poems to convey admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted vice minister of rites, he refused the post, sent up seven memorials, and offered archaic verse as veiled remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知福州，再以侍郎召，為台臣所沮而止。

translations.literal: After a long time he was called up to govern Fuzhou; summoned again as vice minister, he was blocked by censoriate officials and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled to govern Fuzhou; when the court tried again to summon him as vice minister, censorial officials blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遂守寶章閣待制致仕，卒諡文恭。

translations.literal: He then held attendant of Baozhang Pavilion and retired; upon death he was given the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as attendant of Baozhang Pavilion and retired; after his death he was posthumously titled Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子愉老，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Yu Lao also passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu Lao likewise earned the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 王萬，字處一，家世婺州，父遊淮間，萬因生長濠州。

translations.literal: Wang Wan, style name Chuyi, his family for generations was from Wuzhou; his father traveled the Huai region, and Wan thus grew up in Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan, styled Chuyi, came of a Wuzhou family; because his father worked along the Huai, he was raised in Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 少忠伉有大誌，究心當世急務，尤精於邊防要害。

translations.literal: In youth he was loyal and upright with great aspiration; he devoted his heart to the urgent affairs of the age and was especially expert in the key points of border defense.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was forthright and ambitious, bent on the pressing problems of the day, with a special mastery of frontier strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 登嘉定十六年進士第，調和州教授。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the sixteenth year of Jiading and was assigned professor of He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiading 16 (1223) and was posted as professor at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，主管尚書吏部架閣文字，遷國子學錄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he superintended archival documents of the Ministry of Personnel and was moved to recorder of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Duanping 1 (1234) he oversaw the Ministry of Personnel archives and was promoted recorder of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 明年，添差通判鎮江府。

translations.literal: The next year he received additional duty as vice prefect of Zhenjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was given additional duty as vice prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 時金初滅，當路多知其人豪也，谘問者旁午。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin had just been destroyed; those in power mostly knew he was a man of talent, and inquirers came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jin newly fallen, men at court knew him for a strategist, and consultations crowded his days.

sentences.zh: 鄭清之初謀乘虛取河洛，萬謂當急為自治之規。

translations.literal: Zheng Qingzhi at first plotted to seize the moment and take the He and Luo regions; Wan said one should urgently lay down rules of self-governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Qingzhi first planned to exploit the vacuum and recover Henan, Wan urged that the court first put its own house in order.

sentences.zh: 已而大元兵壓境。

translations.literal: Soon after, Great Yuan troops pressed the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the armies of the Great Yuan were on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 三邊震動，理宗下罪己詔，吳泳起草，又以谘萬， 萬謂：“兵固失矣，言之甚，恐亦不可。

translations.literal: The three frontiers shook; Emperor Lizong issued a self-blame edict, Wu Yong drafted it, and again consulted Wan. Wan said, "The army has indeed failed; to speak of it too strongly, I fear, is also not possible.
translations.idiomatic: Alarm ran along all three frontiers. Emperor Lizong issued an edict of self-reproach, drafted by Wu Yong, and again sought Wan's counsel. Wan replied, "Our forces have indeed suffered defeat, but to dwell on it at length in public may do more harm than good.

sentences.zh: 今邊民生意如發，宜以振厲奮發，興感人心。

translations.literal: Now the livelihood of border people is stretched taut as a bowstring; one should use stirring vigor to rouse and move people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The border folk are stretched to the breaking point; the edict should rouse their spirit and win back their hearts."

sentences.zh: ”為條具沿邊事宜，遍告大臣要官，謂：“長淮千里，中間無大山澤為限，擊 首尾應，正如常山蛇勢，首當並兩淮為一製閫之命是聽。

translations.literal: " He drew up border affairs item by item and told them everywhere to great ministers and key officials, saying, "The Long Huai stretches a thousand li with no great mountains or marshes between as a barrier; strike the head and the tail responds, just like the Mount Chang serpent formation. The head should merge the Two Huai into one military commission whose command all obey.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out frontier policy in detail and pressed it on every senior minister, arguing that the thousand-li Huai line had no mountain barrier: strike one point and the whole line must answer, like the serpent of Mount Chang. The first step was to unite the Two Huai under a single commander.

sentences.zh: 兩淮惟濠州居中。

translations.literal: Of the Two Huai, only Haozhou sits in the center.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Two Huai, only Haozhou stands at the center.

sentences.zh: 濠之東為盱眙，為楚，以達鹽城，淮流深廣，敵所難度。

translations.literal: East of Hao is Xuyi, which is Chu, reaching Yancheng; the Huai current is deep and broad, and the enemy finds it hard to cross.
translations.idiomatic: East of Haozhou lies Xuyi in the Chu sector, the route toward Yancheng; there the Huai runs deep and wide and the enemy can hardly ford it.

sentences.zh: 濠之西為安豐，為光，以達信 陽，淮流淺澀，敵每揭厲以涉之。

translations.literal: West of Hao is Anfeng, which is Guang, reaching Xinyang; the Huai current is shallow and obstructed, and the enemy often hikes up their clothes to wade across.
translations.idiomatic: West of Haozhou is Anfeng in the Guang sector, the road to Xinyang; there the Huai is shallow and sluggish, and the enemy regularly wades it with garments hitched up.

sentences.zh: 法當調揚州北軍三千人，自淮東搗虛，常往來宿、亳間，使敵無意於東，而我並力淮西。

translations.literal: By regulation one should deploy three thousand northern troops of Yangzhou, from Huai east strike at the void, and constantly move between Suzhou and Bozhou, so that the enemy has no mind for the east while we combine strength in Huai west.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed to shift three thousand northern troops from Yangzhou to raid from the Huai east, shuttling between Suzhou and Bozhou so the enemy would not fix on the eastern bank while Song concentrated on the Huai west.

sentences.zh: 淮西則又惟合肥居江、淮南北之中，法當 建製置司合肥，而以濠梁、安豐、光州為臂，以黃岡為肘後緩急之助。

translations.literal: In Huai west, again only Hefei sits between the Jiang and the Huai, north and south; by regulation one should establish a Pacification Commission at Hefei, with Haoliang, Anfeng, and Guangzhou as the arms, and Huanggang as elbow and rear for urgent or slow aid.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai west only Hefei lies midway between the Yangzi and the Huai; there he would seat the Pacification Commission, with Haoliang, Anfeng, and Guangzhou as its arms and Huanggang as the reserve behind the elbow.

sentences.zh: 又必令荊、襄每候西兵東來，輒尾之，使淮、襄之勢亦合，而後大規模可立。”

translations.literal: Again one must make Jing and Xiang whenever they observe western troops coming east immediately tail them, so that the momentum of Huai and Xiang also unites, and only then can a large-scale plan be established.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Xiang must watch for western armies moving east and dog their march, so the Huai and Xiang fronts would join--only then could a grand strategy take shape.

sentences.zh: 論用兵，則謂：“當以五千人為屯，每屯一將、二長，一大將一路，又合一大將而並合於製置為總統。

translations.literal: On employing troops he said, "One should take five thousand men as an encampment; each encampment has one general and two leaders; one great general for one route; again combine great generals and merge them under the Pacification Commission as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: On tactics he proposed units of five thousand, each with one general and two captains; a route commander over them, and all route commanders under the Pacification commissioner as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 淮東可精兵三萬，光、黃可二萬，東西夾擊，而沿江製司會合 肥兵共二萬，以牽製其中。

translations.literal: Huai east could have thirty thousand elite troops, Guang and Huang twenty thousand, striking east and west in pincer; while the along-river Pacification Commission joins Hefei troops totaling twenty thousand to pin the center.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand picked troops on the Huai east, twenty thousand at Guang and Huang to strike in concert from east and west, and twenty thousand from the riverine command and Hefei to fix the enemy in the center.

sentences.zh: 行則給營陣，止則依城壘；

translations.literal: On the march supply camp arrays; at halt rely on ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: On campaign they would carry field encampments; at rest they would shelter in walled posts;

sentences.zh: 行則齎幹糧，止則就食州縣。

translations.literal: on the march carry dry provisions; at halt take food from prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: on the march they would bear dry rations, and in garrison draw supplies from local prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: ”論屯田，則謂：“當於新復州軍，東則海、邳，所依者水之險，西則唐、鄧， 所依者山之險，畫此無地無田不耕，則歸附新軍流落餘民亦有固誌。”

translations.literal: " On garrison fields he said, "In the newly recovered prefectures and armies, in the east Hai and Pi, what they rely on is the danger of water; in the west Tang and Deng, what they rely on is the danger of mountains. Mark this so that no land and no field go uncultivated, and then returned subjects, new armies, and scattered remaining people will also have firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " On garrison agriculture he urged that in every recovered prefecture--Hai and Pi in the east with water as their defense, Tang and Deng in the west with mountains--every scrap of land be brought under the plow, so refugees and surrendered troops would have reason to stay.

sentences.zh: 又謂：“戎司舊分地戍守，殿步兵戍真、揚、六合，鎮江兵戍揚、楚、盱眙，建 康馬司兵戍滁、濠、定遠，都統司兵戍廬、和、安豐，以至池司兵戍舒、蘄、巢縣，江司兵戍蘄、黃、浮光，地勢皆順，皆以統製部之出外，而皆常有帥臣居內，以 本軍財賦葺營柵，撫士卒，備器械，以故軍事常整辦。

translations.literal: He again said, "The military offices formerly divided territory for garrison defense: Palace Foot soldiers garrisoned Zhen, Yang, and Liuhe; Zhenjiang troops garrisoned Yang, Chu, and Xuyi; Jiankang Horse Bureau troops garrisoned Chu, Hao, and Dingyuan; Metropolitan Command troops garrisoned Lu, He, and Anfeng; down to Chizhou Command troops garrisoning Shu, Qi, and Chaoxian, and Jiang Command troops garrisoning Qi, Huang, and Fuguang--the terrain in each case was favorable, all placed under unified control and sent outward, while commanders always stayed within, using their army's revenue to repair camps and palisades, comfort soldiers, and prepare weapons; thus military affairs were regularly in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled how each command once held its own sector: Palace Foot at Zhen, Yang, and Liuhe; Zhenjiang troops on the Yang and Chu line through Xuyi; Jiankang cavalry at Chu, Haozhou, and Dingyuan; metropolitan forces at Lu, He, and Anfeng; and so on through Chizhou and Jiang commands at their proper posts. Terrain dictated deployment; a commander stayed home to spend his command's funds on walls, pay the ranks, and stock arms--and the frontier stayed ready.

sentences.zh: 遇警急則帥臣親統重兵以行。

translations.literal: When alarm was urgent the commander personally led heavy troops on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis came the commander himself led the main force out.

sentences.zh: 比乃有以建康馬帥而知黃州者，都統而知光州者，以池司都統而在楚州，以鎮江 都統而在應天者，將不知兵，兵不屬將，往往以本軍之財，資他處之用，以致營柵壞而莫修，士卒貧而莫給，器械鈍而莫繕，宜與盡還舊制。

translations.literal: Now there are cases of a Jiankang cavalry commander governing Huangzhou, a metropolitan commander governing Guangzhou, a Chizhou metropolitan commander in Chuzhou, a Zhenjiang metropolitan commander in Yingtian--generals do not know troops, troops do not belong to generals; often the revenue of one army funds uses elsewhere, so that camps and palisades decay with none to repair them, soldiers are poor with none to supply them, and weapons are dull with none to sharpen them. The old system should all be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Now a cavalry commander from Jiankang might govern Huangzhou, a metropolitan commander Guangzhou, a Chizhou commander sit in Chuzhou, a Zhenjiang commander in Yingtian--generals estranged from their men, men from their paymasters. One command's funds built another's posts; ramparts crumbled, soldiers went unpaid, arms rusted untouched. He pleaded to restore the old order.

sentences.zh: ”及請寬邊民，請團民 兵，請援浮光，請邊民之能捍邊者，常厚其賞而小其官，使常得其力。

translations.literal: " He also requested easing the border people, organizing civilian militia, aiding Fuguang, and for border people able to defend the border, often enriching their rewards and shrinking their offices, so as always to obtain their strength.
translations.idiomatic: " He also asked relief for frontier households, militia musters, aid for Fuguang, and generous pay with modest rank for local defenders who could hold the line.

sentences.zh: 其後兵興用窘，履畝之令行，則又言之廟堂曰：“今名更化，可反為故相之所不為乎？

translations.literal: Afterward war arose and funds were strained; the field-measurement order was enacted, and he again spoke in the court hall, saying, "Now we are styled 'Renewal and Transformation'--can we turn back to what the former chief minister would not do?
translations.idiomatic: When war strained the treasury and the field-survey tax was imposed, he rose again in court: "The reign is called Renewal and Transformation--will we repeat what the former chief minister would not do?"

sentences.zh: ”其他 敷陳，往往累數萬言，其自任之篤，切於當世如此。

translations.literal: " His other presentations often accumulated tens of thousands of words; his self-assumption was so earnest and so pressing on the age in this way.
translations.idiomatic: " His other memorials often ran to tens of thousands of words; he charged himself with the age in just this spirit.

sentences.zh: 三年。

translations.literal: Third year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the era.

sentences.zh: 授樞密院編修官。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙六年，兼權屯田郎中，因轉對，言：“天命去留原於君心，陛下一一 而思之，凡惻然有觸於心而未能安者，皆心之未能同乎天者也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaxi, concurrently acting director of the Garrison Fields Bureau, on rotated audience he said, "Whether Heaven's mandate stays or goes originates in the ruler's heart. Your Majesty, thinking one by one, every matter that stirs the heart with unease that cannot be settled--all are cases where the heart has not yet matched Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 6 (1246), while acting director of garrison fields, he spoke on rotated audience: "Heaven's favor rests on the ruler's heart. Your Majesty, weigh each doubt that pricks your conscience--every unease is a sign that heart and Heaven are not yet one.

sentences.zh: 天不在天，而在陛下之心，苟能天人合一，永永勿替，天命在我矣。

translations.literal: Heaven is not in Heaven but in Your Majesty's heart; if heart and Heaven can unite, forever without ceasing, Heaven's mandate is in us.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is not above us but within Your Majesty's heart; if ruler and Heaven become one and never part, the mandate is ours again."

sentences.zh: ”差知台州，至郡日，惟蔬飯， 終日坐廳事，事至立斷，吏無所售，往往改業散去，民亦化之不復訟，上下肅然，郡以大治。

translations.literal: " Assigned to govern Taizhou, on the day he reached the prefecture he ate only vegetable rice, sat in the hall all day, decided matters as they came, clerks had nowhere to peddle influence and often changed profession and dispersed; the people were also transformed and no longer litigated. Above and below were solemn, and the prefecture was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Posted prefect of Taizhou, he took office on nothing but plain vegetables, sat in the yamen from dawn to dusk, and settled each case on the spot. Clerks found no market for graft and drifted away; the people followed his example and lawsuits dwindled. The prefecture grew orderly and thrived.

sentences.zh: 才五月，乞祠去。

translations.literal: After only five months he requested a temple stipend post and left.
translations.idiomatic: After only five months he asked leave on a temple stipend and departed.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷屯田員外郎兼編修，轉對，言：“君臣上下 盡克私心，以服人心，以回天心。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to vice director of garrison fields and concurrent compiler; on rotated audience he said, "Ruler and ministers above and below should all overcome private hearts to win people's hearts and turn back Heaven's heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted vice director of garrison fields and compiler; on audience he urged that court and officials alike shed private interest to win the people and move Heaven.

sentences.zh: ”遷尚右郎官，尋兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: " He was moved to vice director of the Shangyou Bureau and soon concurrently lecturer at Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " He was shifted to the Shangyou Bureau and soon made lecturer at Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was raised investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 首論史宅之，故相之子，曩者弄權，不當復玷從班。

translations.literal: He first memorialized on Shi Zaizhi, son of a former chief minister, who formerly wielded power and should not again stain the attendant ranks.
translations.idiomatic: His first target was Shi Zaizhi, son of a former chief minister who had once abused power; he should not again soil the inner court.

sentences.zh: 上命丞相 再三諭旨，迄不奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief minister repeatedly to convey the edict, but to the end he did not obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the chief minister repeat the order again and again, yet Wan would not yield.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，出宅之知平江府。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no alternative, sent Zaizhi out as prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: At last the throne sent Zaizhi out to govern Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 又論之，疏凡五上，史嵩之自江上董師入相，萬又首論之，謂其“事體迫遽，氣象傾搖，太學生欲趣其歸，則賄 賂之跡已形。

translations.literal: He again memorialized on him; memorials in all were submitted five times. Shi Songzhi, supervising the army on the river, entered as chief minister; Wan again first memorialized on him, saying his "affairs were pressing and urgent, the atmosphere leaning and swaying; when Imperial University students wished to hurry his return, traces of bribery had already appeared.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack in five more memorials. When Shi Songzhi left the river front to become chief minister, Wan led the opposition, charging that "his conduct was rash, the court unsteady; when students demanded his recall, the trail of bribes was already plain.

sentences.zh: 近或謂有族人發其私事，肆為醜詆者，以相國大臣而若此，非書之所謂大臣矣”。

translations.literal: Recently some say a clansman exposed his private affairs and wantonly made ugly slander--for a grand minister and chief minister to be like this is not what the classics call a minister."
translations.idiomatic: Some now say kinsmen aired his secrets and he answered with vilification--for a man styled chief minister of the state, this is not the minister the classics mean."

sentences.zh: 然當時論相之事已決，疏入，遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: Yet at the time the matter of criticizing the chief minister was already decided; when the memorial entered he was moved to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: By then the court had already settled on Songzhi; when the memorial arrived Wan was transferred to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 萬即日還常熟寓舍。

translations.literal: Wan that same day returned to his lodgings in Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: That day Wan went home to his lodging in Changshu.

sentences.zh: 遷太 常少卿，辭。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he declined.

sentences.zh: 差知寧國府，辭。

translations.literal: Given additional duty to govern Ningguo prefecture, he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Offered Ningguo prefecture, he declined again.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在奏事，出為福建提點刑獄，加直煥章閣、四川宣諭司參議官，皆力辭，乞休致。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital to report on affairs, sent out as Fujian judicial intendant, with additions of Direct Huanshang Pavilion and staff officer of the Sichuan Pacification Commission--he forcefully declined all and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court, then offered Fujian judicial intendant, Direct Huanshang Pavilion, and a post on the Sichuan pacification staff--he refused each and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔特轉朝奉郎，守太常少卿致仕，卒。

translations.literal: An edict specially promoted him to Court Gentleman for Admonition; he held vice director of sacrifices and retired, then died.
translations.idiomatic: The throne specially promoted him Court Gentleman for Admonition and let him retire as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he died soon after.

sentences.zh: 嵩之 罷相，眾方交論其非，上思萬先見，親賜禦劄，謂萬“立朝蹇諤，古之遺直，為郡廉平，古之遺愛。

translations.literal: When Songzhi was dismissed as chief minister the multitude were just then debating his wrongs; the emperor recalled Wan's foresight and personally bestowed an imperial note, saying of Wan, "Standing at court blunt and forthright--the surviving integrity of antiquity; governing a prefecture honest and fair--the surviving love of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: After Songzhi fell, the court turned on him; remembering Wan's foresight, the emperor sent a personal note: "In office you were blunt and upright, a straight remnant of the ancients; as prefect you were clean and fair, a kindness the ancients would praise.

sentences.zh: 聞其母老家貧，朕甚念之，賜新會五千貫，田五百畝，以贍給其 家。”

translations.literal: Hearing his mother is elderly and his family poor, We greatly remember; We grant five thousand strings of Xinhuizi and five hundred mou of fields to support his household.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing your mother is aged and your household poor, We are moved to grant five thousand strings of Xinhuizi cash and five hundred mou of land for their upkeep.

sentences.zh: 初，萬之學專有得於“時習”之語，謂學莫先於言顧行，言然而行，未然者非言之偽也，習未熟也，熟則言行一矣。

translations.literal: At first Wan's learning had special attainment in the phrase "practice at the proper time"; he said learning has nothing before words that look to conduct--when words are so and conduct follows, what is not yet so is not falsity of words but practice not yet mature; when mature, words and conduct are one.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's thought rested on the Analects' "practice at the proper time": learning begins when speech looks to deed; if words are true the act will follow, and what lags is not hypocrisy but habit still unformed--once formed, word and act are one.

sentences.zh: 故終其身，行無不顧其言。

translations.literal: Therefore throughout his life in conduct there was none that did not look to his words.
translations.idiomatic: All his life his deeds answered his words.

sentences.zh: 發於設施論諫，皆根於中心。

translations.literal: What issued in implementation, discussion, and remonstrance all rooted in his center.
translations.idiomatic: What he proposed, argued, and remonstrated all sprang from the same inward root.

sentences.zh: 遺文有《時習編》及其他奏劄及論天下事者凡十卷。

translations.literal: Surviving writings include the 《Shixi Bian》 and other memorials and discussions of affairs under Heaven, ten juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: His literary remains include the 《Compilation on Practice》 and other memorials on affairs of the realm, ten juan in all.

sentences.zh: 馬光祖，字華父，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Ma Guangzu, style name Huafu, was a native of Jinhua in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guangzu, styled Huafu, was from Jinhua in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 寶慶二年進士，調新喻主簿，已有能名。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Baoqing, he was assigned recorder of Xinyu and already had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Baoqing 2 (1226), served as recorder at Xinyu, and was already known for competence.

sentences.zh: 從真德秀學。

translations.literal: He followed Zhen Dexiu in study.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of Zhen Dexiu.

sentences.zh: 改知餘幹縣，差知高郵軍，遷軍器監主簿，差充督視行府參議官。

translations.literal: Changed to magistrate of Yugan county, given additional duty to govern Gaoyou army, moved to registrar of the Directorate of Armaments, and given additional duty as staff officer of the supervisory headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Made magistrate of Yugan, then acting prefect of Gaoyou, registrar in the Armaments Directorate, and staff officer on the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 奉雲台 祠。

translations.literal: He received the Yuntai temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Yuntai temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 差知處州，監登聞鼓院，進太府寺丞兼莊文府教授、右曹郎官。

translations.literal: Given additional duty to govern Chuzhou, supervised the Petition Drum Court, and advanced to vice director of the Grand Treasury and concurrent professor of Zhuangwen Palace and vice director of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Chuzhou on additional duty, oversaw the Petition Drum Court, and rose to vice director of the Grand Treasury with posts at Zhuangwen Palace and in the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出知處州，乞降僧道牒振濟，詔從之。

translations.literal: Sent out to govern Chuzhou, he requested lowering monastic and Daoist certificates for relief; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Chuzhou he asked to sell monastic and Daoist ordination certificates for famine relief, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 加直秘閣，浙東提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was given Direct Secretarial Pavilion and made Zhedong intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Direct Secretarial Pavilion, he became Zhedong intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 移浙西提點刑獄，時暫兼權浙 西提舉常平。

translations.literal: Transferred to Zhexi judicial intendant, at the time temporarily also acting Zhexi intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Zhexi as judicial intendant, for a time also acting intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries there.

sentences.zh: 起復軍器監、總領淮東軍馬錢糧兼知鎮江。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning to the Directorate of Armaments, he was overall commander of Huaidong army horses, funds, and grain and concurrently governed Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning to the Armaments Directorate, he took charge of Huaidong funds and supplies while governing Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 進直徽猷閣、江西轉運副使兼知隆興府。

translations.literal: Advanced to Direct Huixian Pavilion, Jiangxi transport vice commissioner and concurrently prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Huixian Pavilion, he became Jiangxi transport vice commissioner and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 以右正言劉漢弼言罷。

translations.literal: On the words of Remonstrator of the Right Liu Hanbi he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed after Remonstrator of the Right Liu Hanbi attacked him.

sentences.zh: 後九年，起直徽猷閣、知太平州、提領江西 茶鹽所。

translations.literal: Nine years later he was called up as Direct Huixian Pavilion, governed Taiping prefecture, and supervised the Jiangxi Tea and Salt Office.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later he returned as Direct Huixian Pavilion, prefect of Taiping, and head of the Jiangxi tea and salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 進直寶文閣，遷太府少卿，仍知太平州、提領江、淮茶鹽所。

translations.literal: Advanced to Direct Baowen Pavilion, moved to vice director of the Grand Treasury, still governing Taiping and supervising the Jiang and Huai Tea and Salt Office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct Baowen Pavilion and vice director of the Grand Treasury while keeping Taiping and the Jiang-Huai tea and salt office.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿、淮西總領兼權江東轉運使。

translations.literal: Moved to director of the Ministry of Agriculture, overall commander of Huai west, and concurrently acting Jiangdong transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Ministry of Agriculture, Huai west overall commander, and acting Jiangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 拜戶部尚書兼知臨安府、浙西安撫使。

translations.literal: Appointed minister of revenue and concurrently prefect of Lin'an and Zhexi pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of revenue, prefect of Lin'an, and Zhexi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝 諭丞相謝方叔趣入覲，乞嚴下海米禁，曆陳京師艱食、和糴增價、海道致寇三害。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Minister Xie Fangshu to hurry him to audience; he requested strict enforcement of the sea-rice ban and set forth in sequence the three harms of capital food hardship, harmonized purchase price increases, and sea routes inviting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Chief Minister Xie Fangshu to bring him in at once; he asked a strict ban on rice by sea and laid out three evils: famine prices in the capital, inflated state grain purchases, and pirates drawn by coastal traffic.

sentences.zh: 加寶章閣直學士、沿江製置使、江東安撫使、知建康府兼行宮留守兼節製和州無為 軍安慶府三郡屯田使，加煥章閣，尋加寶章閣學士。

translations.literal: He was given Academician of Baozhang Pavilion, along-river Pacification Commissioner, Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner, prefect of Jiankang and concurrent palace custodian, and concurrently controller of garrison fields for the three prefectures of Hezhou, Wuwei army, and Anqing--added Huanshang Pavilion, and soon added Academician of Baozhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Made Academician of Baozhang Pavilion, he became riverine Pacification Commissioner, Jiangdong pacifier, and prefect of Jiankang with custody of the traveling palace and garrison-field authority over Hezhou, Wuwei, and Anqing; he was soon also raised to Huanshang and Baozhang academies.

sentences.zh: 始至官，即以常例公用器皿錢二十萬緡支犒軍民，減租稅，養鰥寡孤疾無告之人，招兵置砦，給錢助諸軍昏嫁。

translations.literal: When he first reached office he immediately used the regular public-service vessel money of two hundred thousand strings to pay rewards to army and people, reduced rent and tax, supported widows, orphans, the solitary, the ill, and those with none to appeal to, recruited troops and set stockades, and gave money to aid marriage among the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he spent two hundred thousand strings of the usual public-service fund to reward troops and civilians, cut rents and taxes, cared for widows, orphans, and the destitute, raised troops and built stockades, and gave cash for soldiers' weddings.

sentences.zh: 屬縣稅折收絲綿絹帛，倚閣除免以數萬計。
