translations.literal: In subordinate counties taxes commuted to silk, cotton, and silk cloth were suspended and remitted in sums of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the counties he deferred or remitted taxes taken in silk and cloth, to the tune of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 興學校，禮賢才，辟召僚屬，皆極一時之選。

translations.literal: He revived schools, honored worthy talent, and recruited staff--all were the choicest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He revived schools, honored talent, and recruited aides who ranked among the best men of the day.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、荊湖製置、知江陵府，去而建康之民思之不 已。

translations.literal: Appointed Academician of Duanming Hall, Jinghu Pacification Commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling; when he left, the people of Jiankang longed for him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Made Academician of Duanming Hall, Jinghu pacifier, and prefect of Jiangling, he left Jiankang to a populace that would not forget him.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，命以資政殿學士、沿江製置大使、江東安撫使再知建康，士女相慶。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and ordered him as Academician of Zizheng Hall, great along-river Pacification Commissioner, and Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner to govern Jiankang again; men and women congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, the emperor sent him back as Academician of Zizheng Hall, grand riverine pacifier, and Jiangdong pacifier at Jiankang; the city rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 光祖益思寬養民力，興廢起壞，知無不為，蠲除前政逋負錢百餘萬緡，魚利稅課悉罷 減予民，修建明道、南軒書院及上元縣學。

translations.literal: Guangzu all the more thought to ease and nurture the people's strength, revive what was abandoned and raise what was ruined, and in knowing there was nothing he did not do; he remitted more than a million strings of arrears from the previous administration, entirely abolished and reduced fish-profit tax levies for the people, and built Mingdao and Nanxuan academies and the Shangyuan county school.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu devoted himself to sparing the people and restoring what had decayed, leaving nothing undone: he canceled over a million strings of debt left by his predecessor, cut fish taxes to the bone, and rebuilt Mingdao Academy, Nanxuan Academy, and the Shangyuan county school.

sentences.zh: 扌尊節費用，建平糴倉，貯米十五萬石，又為庫貯糴本二百餘萬緡，補其折閱，發糴常減於市價，以利小民。

translations.literal: He economized expenses, built a level-purchase granary storing one hundred fifty thousand shi of rice, and also a treasury storing more than two million strings of purchase capital; he made up shortfalls, and when grain was released for sale it was always below market price to benefit the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He economized expenses, opened a public granary with a hundred fifty thousand shi of rice in store and a fund of more than two million strings for purchases; he covered losses on sales and regularly sold grain below market price to help the poor.

sentences.zh: 修飭武備， 防拓要害，邊賴以安。

translations.literal: He repaired and ordered military preparations, defended and extended key points, and the border relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He put the defenses in order and secured the critical passes, and the frontier grew calm under his hand.

sentences.zh: 其為政寬猛適宜，事存大體。

translations.literal: In governing he balanced leniency and severity appropriately and kept to the larger principles of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In office he balanced leniency and severity as the situation required and always kept the larger principles in view.

sentences.zh: 公田法行，光祖移書賈似道言公田法非便，乞不以及江東，必欲行之，罷光祖乃可。

translations.literal: When the public-field law was put into effect, Guangzu wrote to Jia Sidao saying the public-field law was not expedient and begged that Jiangdong not be included; if it must be carried out, Guangzu would have to be dismissed first.
translations.idiomatic: When the public-field law took effect, Guangzu wrote to Jia Sidao that the measure was ill-advised and asked that Jiangdong be exempt; if it had to proceed, he said, remove him first.

sentences.zh: 進大學士兼淮 西總領。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Academician while also serving as overall controller of Huai-West.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand academician while also serving as overall controller of Huai-West.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，遷提領戶部財用兼知臨安府、浙西安撫使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the mobile court and transferred to supervise the Ministry of Revenue's finances while also governing Lin'an Prefecture and serving as Zhexi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the mobile court and made supervisor of the Ministry of Revenue's finances while also governing Lin'an and serving as Zhexi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，榮王府積粟不發廩，光祖謁王，辭以故，明日往，亦如之，又明日又往，臥客次，王不得已 見焉。

translations.literal: When famine struck, the Prince of Rong's household had grain stored but would not open the granaries. Guangzu called on the prince, who excused himself on some pretext. Guangzu went again the next day with the same result, and again the day after, lying down in the guest quarters until the prince had no choice but to see him.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine the Prince of Rong hoarded grain and would not release it. Guangzu called on him and was put off with excuses. He returned the next day and the day after, finally lying down in the antechamber until the prince was forced to receive him.

sentences.zh: 光祖厲聲曰：“天下孰不知大王子為儲君，大王不於此時收人心乎？

translations.literal: Guangzu said in a stern voice: "Who in the realm does not know that the great prince is the heir? Will Your Highness not win people's hearts at a time like this?
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu said sharply, "Everyone knows you are the heir apparent. Will you not win the people's hearts now?

sentences.zh: ”王以無粟辭；

translations.literal: " The prince pleaded that he had no grain;
translations.idiomatic: " The prince pleaded that he had no grain;

sentences.zh: 光祖探懷中文書曰：“某莊某倉若干。

translations.literal: Guangzu drew documents from his breast and said: "Such-and-such estate, such-and-such granary, so many units.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzu drew papers from his robe and read, "Such-and-such estate, such-and-such granary, so much grain.

sentences.zh: ”王無以辭，得粟活民甚多。

translations.literal: " The prince had no reply and released grain, saving a great many people.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince could not answer and released the grain, keeping a great many people alive.

sentences.zh: 進同 知樞密院事，尋差知福州、福建安撫使，以侍御史陳堯道言罷，以前職提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then assigned to govern Fuzhou and serve as Fujian Pacification Commissioner. On the memorial of Attending Censor Chen Yaodao he was dismissed and made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then sent to govern Fuzhou and serve as Fujian pacification commissioner. Attending Censor Chen Yaodao had him removed, and he was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 再以沿江製置、江東安撫使知建康，郡民為建祠六所。

translations.literal: He was again made Riverine Pacification Commissioner and Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner while governing Jiankang, and the people of the prefecture built six shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made riverine pacification commissioner and Jiangdong pacification commissioner while governing Jiankang, and the people erected six shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to retire but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire but was refused.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳三 年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianchun he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianchun he was appointed vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜知樞密院事兼參知政事，以監察御史曾淵子言罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as Vice Grand Councilor, but was dismissed on the memorial of Supervising Censor Zeng Yuanzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made director of the Bureau of Military Affairs while also serving as vice grand councilor, but Supervising Censor Zeng Yuanzi had him removed.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧鉞復繳奏新命，以金紫光祿大夫致仕，卒，諡莊敏。

translations.literal: The Supervising Secretary Lu Yue again returned the new appointment with a memorial. He retired as Grand Master of the Golden Purple and Golden Radiance, died, and was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lu Yue returned the new appointment with a memorial. He retired as grand master of the golden purple and golden radiance, died, and was posthumously titled Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 光祖之在外，練兵豐財；

translations.literal: When Guangzu was in the provinces he trained troops and enriched the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces Guangzu trained troops and built up revenues;

sentences.zh: 朝廷以之為京尹，則專治浩穰，風績凜然。

translations.literal: when the court made him capital prefect he devoted himself to governing the great metropolis, and his reputation for discipline was formidable.
translations.idiomatic: when the court made him capital prefect he devoted himself to governing the great metropolis, and his stern reputation was widely felt.

sentences.zh: 三至建康，終始一紀，威惠並行，百廢無不修舉雲。

translations.literal: Three times he governed Jiankang, for a full twelve years in all, combining authority and kindness, and there was no neglected undertaking he did not restore—so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Jiankang three times over a full twelve years, combining authority and kindness, and left nothing neglected that he could restore.

sentences.zh: 論曰：吳淵才具優長，而嚴酷累之。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Wu Yuan's talent and capacity were outstanding, but severity weighed him down.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Wu Yuan's talent was outstanding, but his harshness held him back.

sentences.zh: 餘玠意氣豪雄，而誌不克信。

translations.literal: Yu Jie's spirit was bold and heroic, but his aims could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jie was bold and heroic in spirit, but his promises could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 賈似道不用汪立信之策，殆天奪其魄矣。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao did not employ Wang Lixin's plans—perhaps Heaven had taken his wits.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao refused Wang Lixin's plans—as if Heaven had stolen his judgment.

sentences.zh: 向士璧卒厄於似道，宋之不足圖存，蓋可知也。

translations.literal: Xiang Shibi in the end was ruined by Sidao; that Song was not worth planning to preserve may thus be understood.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shibi was destroyed in the end by Sidao; from this one may see that the Song was no longer worth trying to save.

sentences.zh: 胡穎好 毀淫祠，非其中之無慊，不能爾也。

translations.literal: Hu Ying loved to destroy illicit shrines; had he not been inwardly without unease, he could not have acted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Ying delighted in tearing down illicit shrines; only a man inwardly at peace could act so fearlessly.

sentences.zh: 冷應澄安邊之才。

translations.literal: Leng Yingcheng had talent for securing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Yingcheng had a gift for securing the frontier.

sentences.zh: 曹叔遠、王萬皆正人端士。

translations.literal: Cao Shuyuan and Wang Wan were both upright and principled scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuyuan and Wang Wan were men of integrity and principle.

sentences.zh: 馬光祖治建康，逮今遺愛猶在民心，可謂能臣已。

translations.literal: Ma Guangzu governed Jiankang, and to this day the affection he left behind remains in the people's hearts—he may be called a capable minister indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guangzu governed Jiankang, and the affection he left still lives in people's hearts; he may truly be called a capable minister.
